title: Svp, Revenue Operations
summary: The SVP, Revenue Operations will lead BeyondTrust’s global Revenue Operations function across Field Operations, Marketing Operations, and Data Analytics. The role owns forecasting, GTM planning, territory and quota design, data and systems strategy, AI-enabled automation, and cross-functional revenue performance, while partnering with the CFO, CRO, CMO, and Board.
description:
BeyondTrust is a place where you can bring your purpose to life through the work that you do, creating a safer world through our cybersecurity SaaS portfolio.

Our culture of flexibility, trust, and continual learning means you will be recognized for your growth, and for the impact you make on our success. You will be surrounded by people who challenge, support, and inspire you to be the best version of yourself.

BeyondTrust is scaling from ~$550M to $1B+ ARR, and the levers that got us here won't get us there on their own. The SVP, Revenue Operations owns the operating system that makes that growth predictable — one trusted number, a disciplined cadence, and a revenue engine instrumented well enough to run itself. This is the most senior Revenue Operations seat in the company, reporting directly to an operational, GTM-minded CFO rather than into Sales, and partnering closely with the CRO and territory Sales SVPs as primary internal customers. The role encompasses Field Operations (territory and sales team management), Marketing Operations (demand generation and funnel management), and a full Data Analytics team, a function that serves both GTM and the broader organization. 

The Role

This role is a strategic and tactical operator's seat, not a governance-committee seat. You won't run every report or write every line of code yourself; you'll direct and continuously optimize the teams and systems that do, including the Field Operations arm embedded with Sales, Marketing Ops and the Data Analytics arm behind the numbers. Your value is in knowing exactly where the leverage is: which metric to fix first, which process is quietly costing the company a point of retention, which manual workflow should be automated this quarter, not next year.

You'll own forecasting and pipeline analytics, you’ll parter with the CRO and CFO on GTM strategy and long-range planning, territory-quota-capacity-compensation design, full-lifecycle renewals and retention operations, data roadmap and architecture (serving both GTM and the broader organization), and the prioritization of revenue-impacting Salesforce and RevTech investment. You'll also set the pace on AI adoption across the revenue function and the broader data organization, with real hands-on fluency, not just sponsorship, and hold a decisive seat on how the company's systems roadmap gets built.

Success here is measured in speed and clarity: a tighter forecast, cleaner data, a leaner systems backlog, and a sales organization that trusts the number because you built the mechanism that produces it.

What You’ll Do

  • Operating Cadence & Forecast Integrity — Run the weekly/bi-weekly forecasting pipeline review, and quarterly business reviews in partnership with the CRO/CMO. Reconcile field roll-ups with model-driven forecasts into one number, and name gaps with owners and dates attached.
  • GTM Strategy & Planning — Own the architecture of the long-range plan (TAM, segmentation, coverage, geo-expansion) and lead annual/quarterly capacity and revenue planning in lockstep with FP&A and Sales.
  • Territory, Quota & Compensation — Direct territory design, capacity models, quota setting, and incentive-comp mechanics that drive the right rep behavior — and hold the line on Salesforce data quality and pipeline hygiene that the whole system depends on.
  • Data, Analytics & Engineering Leadership — Lead Data Analytics team serving both GTM and the enterprise. Own the data foundation, modern BI platform, predictive modeling and data science and drive the shift from descriptive reporting to decision-ready insight the ELT acts on. Build the systems and team that make the number trustworthy. You direct the roadmap and people strategy; the team builds and ships.
  • Field Operations Leadership — Own Sales Field Operations as an operational arm, directing territory design, capacity management, rep productivity, and coaching mechanisms. Align with the Sales SVPs and CRO on field strategy, resource allocation, and the people/enablement investments that drive quota attainment. Partner closely with Marketing on demand coverage and Sales on execution.
  • Systems Governance & Roadmap Prioritization — Hold a decisive seat on the Lead-to-Cash forum; bring portfolio discipline (a transparent intake/scoring model) to a demand-rich Salesforce and RevTech backlog run by IT and the Salesforce CoE.
  • Marketing & Partner Operations — Own Marketing Operations as an operational arm alongside Field Ops, setting the operating rhythm for funnel health, lead management, lead scoring, win rate improvement targets, lead-to-sales SLAs, campaign attribution, and partner/channel scorecards. Ensure demand generation, pipeline flow, and revenue reconcile to one integrated model. Work closely with the CMO and CRO on coverage planning.
  • AI-Enabled Revenue Operations — Identify and ship high-leverage automation across forecasting, enablement, sales rep experience and reporting; set the standard for responsible, fast AI adoption across the function.
  • Commercial Operations Partnership — Partner closely with Commercial Operations (deal desk, CPQ, lead-to-order/cash) operating as one engine with clean handoffs and shared data — no reconciliation friction.
  • Team Leadership — Build and develop a high-performing Revenue Operations organization, and represent revenue performance, risk, and opportunity to the CFO, CRO, and Board.

What You’ll Bring

  • 15+ years in Revenue Operations, Sales/Commercial Operations, or GTM strategy within B2B SaaS, including VP/SVP-level leadership partnering with the C-suite and Board.
  • Track record scaling a company through the $550M → $1B+ ARR inflection, or directly comparable scale and complexity.
  • Proven, hands-on ownership of forecasting, planning, and territory/quota/comp design — and a bias for directing the fix, not just diagnosing it.
  • Working fluency in commercial operations (deal desk, CPQ, quote-to-cash) is sufficient to partner effectively without owning the function directly.
  • Experience leading or directly managing both Field Operations (territory, capacity, sales enablement) and Marketing Operations (demand generation, lead management, funnel analytics) at scale, or equivalent cross-functional RevOps scope.
  • Experience leading or chairing a cross-functional systems-governance forum and prioritizing a roadmap against fixed delivery capacity.
  • Power user of Salesforce (or equivalent CRM) and modern RevOps/BI tooling (Gong, Tableau/Power BI, Databricks, Xactly or equivalent) — able to interrogate data directly, without delegation.
  • Personally architected or shipped production of AI, automation, or agentic workflows — a builder's fluency, not just vendor selection.
  • Experience operating in a fast-paced, PE-backed environment.
  • A bachelor's degree is required.

Key Performance Indicators

Success in this seat is tracked with a small set of hard numbers, not a governance scorecard — the candidate should think in terms of what moves each metric and how to align the organization to achieve it.

  • Forecast Accuracy — Quarter-over-quarter variance between forecast and closed bookings held inside target range, across all segments and theatres.
  • Pipeline Health & Data Hygiene — Coverage ratio, stage-conversion rates, and Salesforce data-quality scores trending toward target, not just reported.
  • Net Revenue Retention — Renewal rate, expansion, and churn on a visible, improving trend line.
  • Sales Productivity — Quota attainment %, new-rep ramp time, and capacity-to-plan variance.
  • Systems Throughput — Cycle time on prioritized Salesforce/RevTech initiatives and adoption rate of what ships.
  • AI & Automation Impact — Number of production workflows shipped and measurable hours or cost saved — not tools purchased.
  • Data Reliability — Executive dashboard adoption, account/contact data health, and turnaround time on ELT insight requests.
  • Cross-Functional Trust — CRO, CFO, and ELT confidence in the forecast and in RevOps' recommendations, measured by escalation rate and stakeholder feedback.

Nice to Have

  • Cybersecurity domain experience.
  • Channel-led GTM experience at material scale (MSSP, VAR, GSI, distributor, alliance motions).
  • MBA or a quantitative/engineering background.
  • Experience integrating acquired or newly launched products into an existing GTM motion.
  • Experience supporting marketing and partner operations (funnel/attribution, lead routing, and partner scorecards).

Better Together

Diversity. Inclusion. They’re more than just words for us. They are the guiding values of how we build our teams, cultivate leaders, and create a culture where people feel connected.

We take care of our employees so they can take care of our customers. Customers who come from all walks of life just like us. We hire incredible people from diverse backgrounds because when we are different together, we are stronger together.

About Us

BeyondTrust is the global identity security leader protecting Paths to Privilege™. Our identity-centric approach goes beyond securing privileges and access, empowering organizations with the most effective solution to manage the entire identity attack surface and neutralize threats, whether from external attacks or insiders.

BeyondTrust is leading the charge in transforming identity security to prevent breaches and limit the blast radius of attacks, while creating a superior customer experience and operational efficiencies. We are trusted by 20,000 customers, including 75 of the Fortune 100, and our global ecosystem of partners.

Learn more at www.beyondtrust.com.

summary: BusPatrol is seeking a Vice President of Commercial Operations to lead Sales Enablement and RFP functions and build the operating discipline, tools, training, content, and coordination needed to scale a complex business-to-government commercial motion. The role oversees enablement strategy, sales methodology adoption, deal desk operations, RFP professionalization, competitive intelligence, and performance measurement while aligning Sales, RevOps, Marketing, Legal, Product, Policy/Government Relations, and Post-Sales.
description:
Vice President of Commercial Operations 
 BusPatrol is seeking a high skilled Vice President of Commercial Operations. The VP, Commercial Operations will lead BusPatrol’s Sales Enablement and RFP functions, building the operating discipline, tools, content, training, and cross-functional coordination required to scale a complex B2G commercial motion. This leader will improve seller readiness and execution and professionalizing BusPatrol's RFP engine through clear standard work, stronger workflows, quality controls, and responsible AI adoption. The role will connect Sales, RevOps, Marketing, Policy/Government Relations, Legal, Product, and Post-Sales around a consistent, measurable go-to-market system.
  Responsibilities: 
    Own the Sales Enablement strategy and operating model.   Establish the function’s mandate, roadmap, governance, intake and prioritization process, decision rights, service levels, and annual/quarterly operating cadence in alignment with the company’s commercial strategy.

     Build the training and development architecture.   Lead onboarding, continuous training, manager coaching, launch support, certification, and field reinforcement programs that improve execution in BusPatrol’s complex, multi-stakeholder B2G sales environment.

     Drive sales methodology adoption and field performance.   Embed consistent sales processes, stage expectations, management routines, and practical reinforcement mechanisms that improve execution, deal progression, and seller effectiveness.

     Create and govern the commercial content and tools system.   Ensure that playbooks, stage guidance, talk tracks, battlecards, account-planning tools, stakeholder maps, state/policy guidance, CRM resources, and other field assets are practical, current, reusable, and accessible through a governed source of truth.

     Orchestrate cross-functional GTM alignment and field feedback.   Connect Sales, RevOps, Marketing, Policy/Government Relations, Legal, RFP, Product, and Post-Sales so that commercial insights, process changes, market developments, and frontline feedback are translated into coordinated enablement priorities and field support.

     Establish and operate a commercial deal desk.  Shepherd the last mile of contract execution by coordinating Sales, Legal, Finance, implementation, and installation; resolving deal-execution issues; ensuring commercial and operational readiness; and creating a smooth handoff from closed-won opportunity through delivery

     Lead and professionalize the RFP team.   Improve the quality, consistency, speed, and predictability of RFP responses through standard work, clear workflows, reusable content, response templates, content governance, effective SME coordination, quality controls, and disciplined submission management—while maintaining the team’s core mandate and operating model.

     Build competitive intelligence capability.   Establish repeatable processes for competitive snapshots, account briefs, stakeholder maps, opportunity watchlists, and field-ready competitive guidance that help teams understand market dynamics, competitive posture, and account context.

     Measure impact and drive continuous improvement.   Define and manage performance measures across enablement and RFP operations, including adoption, ramp, manager usage, process adherence, stage conversion, pipeline quality, win-rate contribution, forecast confidence, RFP cycle time, response quality, reuse, and productivity.

   Qualifications: 
   12+ years of progressive experience across sales enablement, commercial operations, sales leadership, Marketing, proposal/RFP operations, or a closely related function

    Demonstrated success building and scaling an enablement operating model, including sales rep onboarding, sales manager enablement, methodology adoption, content governance, certification, field reinforcement, and content performance measurement

    Experience supporting complex B2G, public-sector, GovTech, public safety, or enterprise sales motions involving multiple stakeholders, non-linear procurement, RFPs, and formal approval processes

    Proven leadership of business-to-government deal desk, proposal and/or RFP operations

    Strong cross-functional operating experience partnering with Sales, RevOps, Marketing, Policy/Government Relations, Legal, Product, and Post-Sales to turn strategy and field feedback into adopted processes, tools, and programs

    Fluency with Salesforce and commercial performance data, including pipeline hygiene, stage progression, KPI design, dashboards, and translating analysis into targeted interventions

    Experience using AI and knowledge-management tools to improve research, competitive intelligence, content creation, retrieval, standardization, reuse, and productivity

    Executive-level communication and facilitation skills, with a track record of converting ambiguity into clear priorities, owners, operating rhythms, and measurable outcomes

    Bachelor’s degree required; MBA or equivalent graduate degree preferred (or equivalent practical experience)

   BusPatrol Value Proposition: 
   Who We Are  
 At BusPatrol, safety isn’t just a priority — it’s our mission. As the nation’s most trusted school bus stop-arm technology solution, we serve over 350 school districts, protecting nearly 2 million students across 30,000 buses. Every day, millions of children rely on school buses to get to and from school safely, yet reckless drivers continue to put them at risk.
 As a technology company with a unique focus on public safety, we use cutting-edge AI, machine learning, and telematics to improve school bus safety. Our all-in-one safety program equips school bus fleets with AI-powered cameras, cloud-based data management, and an integrated software platform to capture and process stop-arm violations. Our safety programs foster accountability and reduce dangerous driving behavior in communities across the country.
 By partnering with school districts, municipalities, and law enforcement, we make safety solutions more accessible and effective, ensuring that every child’s journey to and from school is as safe as possible.
   What We Offer  
 When you join BusPatrol, you are not just taking a job. You are joining a mission-driven team dedicated to making a real impact. We offer:
 ✔ Competitive salary and benefits package
 ✔ Unlimited PTO
 ✔ A purpose-driven career, working to protect children and improve public safety
 ✔ The occasion to participate in BusPatrol’s culture of safety, learning, and teamwork
 ✔ A team of innovators, committed to leveraging AI and smart technology for social good
 Be Part of Something Bigger

This is a meaningful opportunity to contribute to a mission-driven company that is using technology to create real change. At BusPatrol, we foster an inclusive and diverse environment built on integrity, collaboration, and innovation. If you are ready to be part of a team that is deeply committed to safety and community impact, we would love to hear from you.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Agentic Commerce & Payments
summary: Replit is seeking a Staff Software Engineer to set the technical direction and build an agentic commerce and payments platform. The role owns architecture and hands-on implementation across purchasing workflows, merchant and service-provider integrations, agent tools, payment lifecycles, provisioning, reliability, security, and enterprise purchasing controls while leading cross-team delivery and mentoring engineers.
description:
Replit is the agentic software creation platform that enables anyone to build applications using natural language. With millions of users worldwide, Replit is democratizing software development by removing traditional barriers to application creation.
 
Make Replit the single place where businesses can buy everything they need through their agents. As a Staff Software Engineer on Replit’s Money team, you’ll set technical direction and build the commerce platform that lets users discover, evaluate, purchase, and manage the products and services they need to build and run their businesses—without leaving Replit.
 Replit already enables businesses to accept payments through integrations such as Stripe. This role builds on that foundation to expand what businesses can buy and accomplish through Replit Agent. You’ll design commerce experiences that combine the simplicity consumers expect with the controls enterprises need, making agent-assisted purchasing useful, trustworthy, and reliable.
 You’ll own architecture and lead cross-team delivery across merchant and service-provider integrations, agent tools, purchasing workflows, and the lifecycle after a transaction. The challenge goes beyond executing a payment: agents need to understand what a user wants, present clear choices and costs, act within delegated authority, and verify that the purchase delivered the intended outcome. You’ll stay hands-on with design and code while aligning partners, mentoring engineers, and turning an ambitious product vision into incremental customer value.

Set the architecture and technical roadmap for agentic commerce, making Replit a single place to discover, buy, and manage the products and services businesses need.
  You will: 
   Lead end-to-end purchasing experiences through Replit Agent: translate user intent into relevant options, communicate prices and terms, obtain appropriate authorization, execute purchases, and confirm fulfillment or provisioning.

  Build extensible integrations with merchants, software vendors, and service providers so the platform can expand its commerce offering without rebuilding each workflow from scratch.

  Build on existing Stripe and payments capabilities, extending payment integrations where needed to support new purchasing experiences rather than treating basic payment acceptance as a greenfield problem.

  Design agent-facing APIs and tools with clear contracts, secure credentials, scoped permissions, spending limits, and appropriate confirmation for consequential actions.

  Partner with product and security to support enterprise purchasing requirements such as role-based access, approval workflows, purchasing policies, and auditable transaction histories, while keeping simpler purchases easy.

  Own the purchase lifecycle beyond checkout: provisioning and access, order and subscription state, receipts, renewals, cancellations, refunds, and reconciliation across providers.

  Make agent-driven transactions reliable with idempotency, verified events, durable state, safe retries, and recovery from partial failures; evaluate whether workflows complete the authorized task without duplicate purchases or unintended spend.

title: Sr. Product Manager, R&d Enablement
summary: Hinge Health is seeking a Senior Product Manager to lead R&D Enablement initiatives and treat internal developer experience as a product. The role owns platform roadmaps across service enablement, mobile app enablement, platform quality, and SRE, while driving AI adoption, developer productivity, quality, observability, knowledge management, and measurable improvements across engineering, product, and design teams.
description:
About Us 
 Hinge Health is pioneering the world's most patient-centered Digital Musculoskeletal (MSK) Clinic. We are building a world-class R&D organization where engineers, product managers, and designers can move fast with confidence, create high-quality solutions, and stay deeply engaged in their work.
  About the Role 
 We are seeking a  Senior Product Manager  to lead our  R&D Enablement  initiatives. In this pivotal role, you will treat our internal developer experience as a product, driving the strategy to achieve P90 industry benchmarks in velocity, throughput, and satisfaction.
 You will oversee the product roadmap for our  Service Enablement, Mobile App Enablement, Platform Quality and SRE pods . Your mandate is to eliminate friction across the entire development lifecycle—from concept and code inception to deployment and observability—empowering our EPD (Engineering, Product, Design) teams to deliver value to our members faster and more reliably.
  Key Responsibilities 
    Define the R&D Enablement Strategy:  Evolve our internal platform strategy from "Engineering Enablement" to broad "R&D Enablement" expanding scope to support Product Managers and Designers along with engineers with AI-powered tools and streamlined workflows.

   Drive the "5 Pillars" of R&D Excellence: 
    AI Adoption:  Lead the integration of AI tools (coding assistants, observability, knowledge management) to automate repetitive tasks and save 5+ hours/week per individual.

   Velocity & Local Iteration:  Champion initiatives like ephemeral environments (Okteto) and CI/CD optimization to drastically reduce lead time for changes.

   Quality Engineering:  Prioritize tooling for flaky test elimination and advanced testing paradigms to reduce production incidents.

   Instrumentation & Observability:  Drive the adoption of structured logging and unified dashboards (DataDog) to democratize production visibility. Ensure our RnD process is well instrumented so that we can measure improvements that process changes & tools bring in.

   Knowledge Management:  Treat documentation as a product, consolidating fragmented knowledge into a centralized, authoritative source.

   Manage the Platform Roadmap:  Partner with Engineering Managers to prioritize technical investments against business value, managing backlogs for Service Enablement, App Enablement, and SRE teams.

   Measure What Matters:  Rigorous tracking of success metrics, including  DXI (Developer Experience Index) ,  PR Throughput ,  DORA metrics , and Mean  Time-to-Recovery (MTTR) .

   Voice of the Customer:  Conduct quarterly DX surveys and "listening tours" to identify friction points and translate feedback into actionable product requirements.

 
   What You'll Do 
   Translate the "RnD Enablement Strategy" into concrete quarterly roadmaps.

  Lead the rollout of a unified  Developer Experience Platform (DXP)  to measure productivity and team performance.

  Collaborate with App Enablement (Mobile DevOps & Mobile App Platform) to optimize the mobile/frontend developer experience, specifically for our Phoenix application stack and release processes.

  Drive cultural change by incentivizing documentation, deep work, and "paved road" adoption across the organization.

  Partner with Security and Infrastructure teams to balance speed with compliance and reliability.

   Basic Qualifications 
    5+ years of Product Management experience , with a strong preference for candidates who have worked on  Internal Developer Platforms (IDP) ,  DevOps tools , or  B2B technical products .

   Technical Fluency:  You can have deep technical conversations with engineers about CI/CD pipelines, microservices architecture, cloud infrastructure (AWS), and mobile release cycles.

   Data-Driven:  Experience using metrics like  DORA ,  SPACE , or  DevEx  to guide decision-making and measure success.

   Program Management:  Strong technical program management skills to orchestrate complex, cross-functional initiatives.

   Change Management:  Proven ability to drive adoption of new tools and processes across a large, distributed engineering organization.

   Preferred Qualifications 
   Working knowledge with our specific tech stack: AWS, Kubernetes,  TypeScript, React Native, Kafka, and DataDog .

  Familiarity with  Backstage (Mission Control)  or similar internal developer portals.

  Experience implementing  GenAI  tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Glean) in an enterprise environment to drive productivity.

  Background in  SRE  or  Platform Engineering  principles.

title: Director, Marketing Technology & Campaign Operations
summary: The Director, Marketing Technology & Campaign Operations leads Arctic Wolf’s global marketing technology ecosystem, data and reporting infrastructure, AI adoption, and campaign operations execution. The role manages Marketo and Salesforce-related systems, campaign delivery across multiple channels and regions, vendor and budget governance, and a distributed team supporting marketing programs.
description:
At Arctic Wolf, you won’t just watch the cybersecurity industry evolve – you'll help lead the change. Our global Pack is made up of people who thrive on solving hard problems, moving fast, and building technology that protects organizations around the world. We’re proud to be recognized by   Forbes, CNBC, Fortune, CRN, Gartner Peer Insights and IDC MarketScape   – but what matters most is the work behind it: delivering real outcomes for customers through award winning innovation like our Aurora Platform.

 If you’re looking for meaningful work, smart teammates and the chance to make a real impact in a high-growth company that’s redefining security operations, Arctic Wolf is the right place for you.

 Our mission is simple: End Cyber Risk. We’re looking for a   Director, Marketing Technology & Campaign Operations    to be a part of making this happen.

    About the Role   
 The Director, Marketing Technology & Campaign Operations owns the technology, data, and operational engine that powers Arctic Wolf’s global marketing organization — from the marketing technology (MarTech) stack and artificial intelligence (AI) roadmap through the campaign operations execution that turns strategy into delivered programs. This role sits on the Growth Services and Operations leadership team and reports directly to the VP, Growth Services and Operations.

 This leader owns the marketing technology ecosystem end to end, including Marketo administration, the broader go-to-market (GTM) technology stack, data architecture and governance, and the effort to embed AI into the team’s core workflows. The role also owns the operational engine that delivers campaigns on behalf of the teams that own strategy and pipeline targets, including Acquisition Marketing, Partner Marketing, Customer Marketing, and demand generation. This is a services and execution role for campaigns — it exists so the teams setting demand strategy have one reliable partner who builds, launches, and runs their programs to a high standard, on time, and within budget. Account-based marketing, pipeline acceleration and reengagement, and creative campaign programs sit outside this role's scope and remain owned by other teams.

 This leader owns campaign execution across email, webinar, direct mail, and content syndication across the NAM (North America), EMEA (Europe, the Middle East, and Africa), and APAC (Asia-Pacific) regions and Arctic Wolf’s sales plays, including the intake model, service level agreements (SLAs), build and QA standards, and the budget and MDF (market development funds) administration that keep the broader marketing organization moving without becoming a bottleneck.

 This is a  people-leadership-heavy  role, managing a distributed team that spans marketing technology, database management, email and nurture strategy, and campaign operations, and a close partner to the Senior Director, Campaigns and Content and the teams that own demand and pipeline targets.

    Responsibilities   

  Marketing Technology Strategy & Architecture
 
  Own the strategy, architecture, and performance of the marketing technology ecosystem, including Marketo administration, governance, and configuration.
 Build and maintain a rolling 12- to 18-month technology roadmap aligned to company growth goals and GTM strategy.
 Own vendor selection, contract negotiation, and renewal decisions for MarTech tools, including intent and enrichment platforms, AI data layers, and integration platform as a service (iPaaS) tools.
 Continuously evaluate emerging technologies and vendors and recommend the highest-return investments.
 Set up, manage, and troubleshoot integrations across the stack, including with Salesforce and other core business systems.
 
  Embedding AI Into Marketing Operations 

  Lead the strategy and execution for embedding AI into the marketing technology stack and daily team workflows.
 Identify and operationalize AI use cases that make marketers and sales development representatives (SDRs) more effective and efficient.
 Own measurable outcomes tied to AI adoption, including cycle-time reduction and process automation, and report progress to leadership.
 Stay ahead of MarTech and AI trends to keep Arctic Wolf’s stack modern and competitive.
 
  Data, Lifecycle & Reporting Infrastructure 

  Own database strategy, lifecycle-stage design, lead scoring, and routing architecture in partnership with the marketing technology and database management team.
 Own the data and reporting infrastructure that supports campaign attribution, sales-play performance, and pipeline reporting.
 Establish data governance and compliance practices (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) that maintain accuracy and consistency across marketing systems.
 Ensure the technology stack is configured for scale, security, compliance, and operational excellence.
 
  Campaign Operations Leadership & Execution Excellence 

  Own the end-to-end campaign operations model across email, webinar (ON24), direct mail (Sendoso), content syndication, and list management, in partnership with the Campaigns and Content team.
 Own the intake model, SLAs, prioritization, and operating cadence that campaign requests move through, including email rules of engagement.
 Ensure consistent build quality, tracking, and attribution setup in Marketo and Salesforce across the NAM, EMEA, and APAC regions and sales plays.
 Continuously identify opportunities to standardize and automate recurring campaign work.
 
  Marketing Investment Planning & Budget Governance 

  Partner with the Revenue and Growth Leadership Team to develop the annual marketing budget, aligning spend with strategic growth priorities and pipeline targets.
 Implement processes and controls to track, approve, and reconcile spend, ensuring budget discipline, transparency, and alignment with corporate finance practices.
 Own budget and MDF administration for the team, including AWS Partner Funding requests, claims, and invoicing.
 
  People Leadership & Team Development 

  Lead and develop a distributed team spanning marketing technology, database management, email and nurture strategy, and campaign operations.
 Set clear priorities, SLAs, operating rhythms, and development plans, including a generalist coverage model so aligned stakeholders never lose a point of contact.
 Build a culture of technical rigor, execution excellence, and continuous improvement.
 
  Cross-Functional Partnership 

  Serve as the primary execution partner to Acquisition Marketing, Partner Marketing, Customer Marketing, and demand generation for their campaign programs.
 Serve as the primary marketing partner to Business Applications and IT, resolving dependencies on routing, scoring, and lifecycle triggers.
 Partner with the Senior Director, Campaigns and Content on campaign calendar, briefs, and content activation.
 Partner with Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, and Finance on shared infrastructure, budget, and vendor decisions.
 Represent marketing technology and campaign operations priorities in Growth Services and Operations leadership planning.
 
    Who You Are   ​
  You are a hands-on technical leader who understands marketing technology architecture at a deep level, and you can run a high-volume campaign execution engine at the same time.
 You see AI as a practical tool for reducing manual work, not a buzzword, and you can identify where it will actually move the needle.
 You build scalable processes, SLAs, and governance rather than absorbing chaos into your own schedule.
 You can manage a distributed, regionally diverse team across both technology and execution disciplines and keep them focused on outcomes, not just tickets.
 You don’t need to own the pipeline number to care about it — you measure yourself by how well you deliver for the teams who do.
 You are comfortable owning a roadmap, a budget, and a vendor negotiation, and just as comfortable being hands-on in the platform or the campaign build when needed.
 
    Minimum Qualifications   
  10+ years of experience in marketing technology, marketing operations, campaign operations, or demand generation, including 3+ years of people leadership.
 Hands-on experience with Marketo (or a comparable marketing automation platform) administration and Salesforce.
 Experience building and owning a marketing technology roadmap, including vendor evaluation, integration management, and stack governance.
 Experience managing multi-channel campaign execution, such as email, webinar, and direct mail, at scale.
 Experience identifying and operationalizing AI or automation use cases within marketing or revenue operations workflows.
 Experience managing distributed or global teams.
 Strong business acumen with the ability to connect marketing technology and campaign investments to revenue outcomes.
 
    Preferred Qualifications   
  Experience in cybersecurity, software as a service (SaaS), or another complex business-to-business (B2B) industry.
 Experience managing a team spanning multiple regions, such as NAM, EMEA, and APAC.
 Marketo certification or an equivalent platform  certification.  
 Experience with intent or data enrichment tooling, such as 6sense, ZoomInfo, or Clay.
 Experience administering a marketing budget or MDF program.
 
   Travel Requirements  
 Typically 10% or less of business travel.

    On-Camera Policy   
   To support a fair, transparent, and engaging interview experience, candidates interviewing remotely are expected to be on camera during all video interviews. 
  Being on camera fosters authentic connection, improves communication, and allows for full engagement from both candidates and interviewers. 
  We understand that technical, bandwidth, or location-related challenges may occasionally prevent video use. If this applies, candidates are required to notify us in advance so we can explore appropriate accommodations. 
 
    About Arctic Wolf   
 At Arctic Wolf, we foster a collaborative and inclusive work environment that thrives on diversity of thought, background, and culture. This is reflected in our multiple awards, including   Top Workplace USA (2021-2025), Best Places to Work – USA (2021-2025), Great Place to Work – Canada (2021-2024), Great Place to Work – UK (2024-2026), and Kununu Top Company – Germany (2024-2026)  . Our commitment to bold growth and shaping the future of security operations is matched by our dedication to customer satisfaction, with over 10,000 customers worldwide and more than 2,000 channel partners globally. As we continue to expand globally and enhance our technology, Arctic Wolf remains the most trusted name in the industry.

    Our Values   
 Arctic Wolf recognizes that success comes from delighting our customers, so we work together to ensure that happens every day. We believe in diversity and inclusion, and truly value the unique qualities and unique perspectives all employees bring to the organization. And we appreciate that—by protecting people’s and organizations’ sensitive data and seeking to end cyber risk— we get to work in an industry that is fundamental to the greater good.

 We celebrate unique perspectives by creating a platform for all voices to be heard through our Pack Unity program. We encourage all employees to join or create a new alliance. See more about our Pack Unity    here   .

 We also believe and practice corporate responsibility, and have recently joined the Pledge 1% Movement, ensuring that we continue to give back to our community. We know that through our mission to End Cyber Risk we will continue to engage and give back to our   communities.   

 All wolves receive compelling compensation and benefits packages, including:  
   Equity for all employees  
  Flexible time off and paid volunteer days  
  401k match 
  Training and career development programs  
  Comprehensive private benefits plan including medical, mental health, dental, disability, life and AD&D, and value-added services  
  Robust Employee Assistance Program (EAP) with mental health services  
  Fertility support and paid parental leave  
 
 Arctic Wolf is an Equal Opportunity Employer and considers applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, orientation, national origin, age, disability, genetics, or any other basis forbidden under federal, provincial, or local law. Arctic Wolf is committed to fostering a welcoming, accessible, respectful, and inclusive environment ensuring equal access and participation for people with disabilities. As such, we strive to make our entire experience as accessible as possible and   provide accommodations as   required for candidates and employees with disabilities and/or other specific needs where possible. Please let us know if you require any accommodation by emailing   recruiting@arcticwolf.com. View   our    Hiring Page    to learn more about our application process.

    Security Requirements   
   Conducts duties and responsibilities in accordance with AWN’s Information Security policies, standards, processes, and controls to protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of AWN business information (in accordance with our employee handbook and corporate policies).  
  Background checks are required  for this position.   
  This position may require access to information protected under U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (“EAR”).  Please note that, if applicable, an offer for employment will be conditioned on authorization to receive software or technology controlled under these U.S. export control laws and regulations.

This range reflects the base pay the company reasonably expects to offer for this position, aligned to the broader job family base pay structure. Actual base pay may vary based on skills, experience, and location, including job family level. In addition to base pay, Arctic Wolf offers variable incentive compensation, new hire equity grants, and a comprehensive benefits package.

description:

Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.

  About the Role: 
 The Red Team Consultant will perform dedicated Red Team activities simulating known threat actors, to help CrowdStrike customers determine the impact and likelihood of threat actors to accomplish objectives across the Kill Chain and MITRE ATT&CK Framework. The Red Team Consultant is expected to be able to coordinate with senior leadership, plan, execute assessments and assist the other CrowdStrike Services’ functions to help improve customers' security defense.

   Perform penetration assessments of operating systems, applications, databases and network infrastructure components to detect, enumerate threats.

   Minimum 3 years of experience in a Red Team/Penetration Testing activities is highly preferred.

  Advanced experience with security assessment tools (Metasploit, NMAP, Cobalt Strike, Nessus, Burp Suite, etc.).

  Comprehensive understanding of the security methodologies, technologies, and best practices.

  Windows / Linux / UNIX / Mac operating systems.

  Advanced experience with Networking components (routers, switches, load balancers, wireless access points, etc.).

  Comprehensive knowledge of firewalls, proxies, mail servers and web servers.

  Advanced experience with operational support for operating systems, applications and networks.

title: Sr. Gtm Engineer, Outbound
summary: SentinelOne is hiring a Senior GTM Engineer, Outbound to build AI agents, automations, integrations, and evaluation systems that improve prospecting, sequencing, deal-signal detection, forecasting, and pipeline hygiene. The senior individual contributor will own portions of the outbound technology stack, implement safeguards, measure quality, and coach SDRs, AEs, and revenue operations teams on AI-enabled workflows.
description:
Our Purpose  
 
 At SentinelOne, we are driven by a clear purpose: to give the advantage to those who secure our future. As AI reshapes how organizations build, operate, and innovate, the responsibility to protect them becomes more critical than ever. When you join SentinelOne, your work helps protect global enterprises, critical infrastructure, and the technologies shaping tomorrow. If you are motivated by meaningful challenges and want your impact to be real, measurable, and global, you will find purpose here.
 About Us  
 
 SentinelOne is a company at the intersection of AI and security, pioneering a new operating model for cybersecurity. Our AI-native platform unifies protection across endpoint, cloud, identity, data, and AI systems to deliver autonomous detection and response with clarity and speed. By combining real-time analytics, intelligent automation, and a unified data foundation, we reduce noise, simplify complexity, and empower security teams to focus on what truly matters.
 Our teams are builders, problem-solvers, and innovators committed to shaping the future of security. If you are excited to solve hard problems alongside talented, mission-driven people, we invite you to help us build a safer future for humanity.
  What Are We Looking For? 
 We’re looking for people who are relentlessly curious and committed to continuous learning. AI is reshaping every function across our business, and we enable every team member, regardless of role or level, to build fluency in AI tools and concepts. Those who thrive here actively seek out new solutions, experiment thoughtfully, and apply what they learn to drive better, faster, smarter outcomes.
  As a Sr. GTM Engineer, Outbound, you will be tasked with building the AI agents, automations, and integrations that speed up prospecting, sharpen targeting, and surface the signals reps need to close, embedded with the SDR and AE organizations. Success is measured in more qualified pipeline per rep, faster deal cycles, and reps who no longer do the manual version of this work. This is a senior individual contributor role where your leverage comes from what you ship, not from managing headcount, and you will set the craft bar for outbound automation and coach SDRs and AEs as you go.
 What Will You Do?
 Primary responsibilities include:
  Automate prospecting by building agents that research accounts, build lists, and draft personalized outreach at scale for SDRs.
 Build sequencing intelligence, designing workflows that optimize send times, cadence steps, and messaging based on engagement data.
 Surface deal signals by building agents that mine call recordings and CRM activity for risk flags, buying signals, and next-best-action recommendations for AEs.
 Own the outbound stack, integrating sales engagement, conversation intelligence, enrichment, and CRM so rep-facing data stays accurate and actionable, for example Outreach/Salesloft, Gong/Chorus, Salesforce, and ZoomInfo/Clearbit.
 Support forecasting and pipeline hygiene by building automations that flag stale deals, missing data, and forecast risk before they become surprises.
 Make quality measurable by building evals for outreach personalization quality, call-summary accuracy, and signal precision against human baselines.
 Build the guardrails, implementing human-in-the-loop review for anything rep- or customer-facing, plus logging and rollback paths.
 Coach and document, bringing SDRs, AEs, and revenue operations up the AI curve and building playbooks and reusable templates.
 Ramp through a staged first year: in months 1 to 3, embed with one or two priority teams, map the current outbound motion end-to-end across prospecting, sequencing, call review, and deal progression, and ship your first prospecting or sequencing automation with an eval harness behind it; in months 4 to 6, deploy a deal-signal or call-intelligence agent live for AEs and stand up shared templates for outreach, personalization, and account research.
 In months 7 to 12, own a meaningful slice of the outbound automation layer, show measurable gains in pipeline per rep, cycle time, and forecast accuracy, and hand off matured systems to SDR and AE leadership so they run day-to-day on the systems you built and instrumented.
  What Skills and Knowledge Will You Bring?
 Ideal candidates will have:
  6 or more years across sales development, sales operations, revenue operations, or systems/solutions engineering, with hands-on time building automation or AI into outbound or sales workflows.
 Demonstrated experience designing, building, and deploying AI agents (prospecting agents, call-summary agents, deal-signal agents) that changed real pipeline or cycle-time outcomes.
 Fluency with the outbound stack and how rep-facing data moves through it, including sales engagement platforms such as Outreach and Salesloft; conversation intelligence such as Gong and Chorus; CRM in Salesforce; forecasting in Clari; enrichment and prospecting through ZoomInfo, Clearbit, and LinkedIn Sales Navigator; and meeting scheduling through Chili Piper.
 Strong prompt architecture skills and practical experience with agent frameworks, orchestration platforms such as n8n and Make, and API/MCP integrations.
 Working proficiency in at least one of SQL, Python, or JavaScript, enough to build lightweight tools, integrations, and workflows.
 A builder's instinct paired with GTM judgment: you understand quota, pipeline coverage, and deal stages, and you prioritize by revenue impact.
 Experience building evaluation frameworks for AI systems (prompt evals, benchmarking, regression testing), and practical experience fine-tuning or heavily customizing models for production use cases, is preferred.
 Familiarity with forecasting methodologies and pipeline hygiene practices is preferred.
 Comfort coaching non-technical teammates through AI adoption and anticipating resistance without relying on positional authority is preferred.
 A B2B or enterprise SaaS background, including familiarity with brand-safety and compliance constraints on automated outputs, is preferred.
  Why SentinelOne?
 AI is redefining how the world operates and rewriting the rules of security in real time, and SentinelOne was built for this moment. From day one, we architected an AI-native platform designed to operate at machine speed, not as an add-on to legacy systems but as the foundation itself. If you want to build where innovation and impact move together, this is that place.

 Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)

 Paid company holidays and paid sick time

 Nationwide pet insurance

 Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.
 Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

title: Senior Manager, Revenue Enablement
summary: Ironclad is seeking a Senior Manager, Revenue Enablement to lead global, field-facing enablement for sales, account management, and customer success teams. The role focuses on scalable enablement programs, AI adoption, value-based selling, product certifications, manager coaching, cross-functional alignment, and metrics tied to business outcomes.
description:
Ironclad is the leading AI contracting platform that transforms agreements into assets. Contracts move faster, insights surface instantly, and agents push work forward, all with you in control. Whether you’re buying or selling, Ironclad unifies the entire process on one intelligent platform, providing leaders with the visibility they need to stay one step ahead. That’s why the world’s most transformative organizations, from Rivian to the World Health Organization and the Associated Press, trust Ironclad to accelerate their business.
 
We’re consistently recognized as a leader in the industry: a Leader in the Forrester Wave and Gartner Magic Quadrant for Contract Lifecycle Management, a Fortune Great Place to Work, and one of Fast Company’s Most Innovative Workplaces. Ironclad has also been named to Forbes’ AI 50 and Business Insider’s list of Companies to Bet Your Career On. We’re backed by leading investors including Accel, Y Combinator, Sequoia, BOND, and Franklin Templeton. For more information, visit  www.ironcladapp.com  or follow us on LinkedIn.


 About the role
 Ironclad is looking for a Senior Manager, Revenue Enablement to lead field-facing enablement for our Revenue organization which includes sales, account management and customer success teams. This is a strategic role for someone who can stay close to the field, translate business priorities into scalable programs, and help our teams adopt new ways of acquiring and growing customers in an increasingly AI-driven environment.
 We are seeking a leader who can combine strong enablement instincts, operational rigor, and AI fluency to improve revenue productivity, strengthen front line manager reinforcement, and drive more consistent execution across the Revenue organization.
 The right person will own broad field enablement motions, including scalable value-selling reinforcement, building organizational confidence with AI tools and AI-era messaging, and driving quarterly product certifications. They will partner closely with Revenue leadership, Product Marketing, Sales Ops, Product, Legal, and other key stakeholders to translate business priorities into lasting behavior change.
 What you’ll do
   Own and evolve scalable global enablement programs that improve productivity, field readiness, and front line manager effectiveness.

  Build practical AI-forward enablement that helps the Revenue org understand and adopt emerging AI capabilities

  Translate Ironclad’s AI and product strategy into clear field sales plays, messaging, and reinforcement that helps the Revenue team position Ironclad’s value effectively in the agentic era.

  Partner closely with Revenue leaders to identify business priorities, surface field gaps, and focus enablement on the highest-value opportunities.

  Reinforce strong discovery, value-based selling, platform pitch quality, and manager coaching through practical programs, workshops, and certifications.

  Help raise the bar on how Ironclad is positioned in the market by equipping the field with stronger AI-era narratives, stronger competitive differentiation, and clearer business-value storytelling.

  Partner cross-functionally with Product, Product Marketing, Sales Ops, Legal, Customer Outcomes, and Enablement peers to align readiness, messaging, and execution.

  Use data, manager feedback, and field signals to identify where sellers are getting stuck and design targeted programs that improve overall performance.

  Define and operationalize success metrics that connect enablement work to meaningful business outcomes, not just completion rates or activity metrics.

  What we’re looking for
   5+ years of experience in Revenue Enablement, Sales Enablement, Revenue Productivity, Sales leadership, or a closely related GTM role.

  Strong fluency with AI tools, workflows, and prompting, plus the ability to turn AI potential into practical field adoption and seller behavior change.

  Experience building and scaling enablement programs that improve execution, not just content delivery.

  A strong understanding of what drives revenue effectiveness, deal progression, pipeline quality, and manager-led coaching.

  Demonstrated experience influencing senior stakeholders and operating effectively in highly cross-functional environments.

  Strong facilitation and program design skills across live, virtual, and on-demand formats.

  A sharp point of view on how to equip sellers for an AI-shaped market, including messaging, differentiation, workflow adoption, and customer conversations.

  Strong communication skills, executive presence, and the ability to bring structure and clarity to fast-moving environments.

  High ownership, strong judgment, and a bias for action.

  Nice to have
   Experience supporting enterprise Sales teams in B2B SaaS or legal tech.

  Experience with manager enablement, certification programs, and reinforcement-based learning models.

  Experience enabling teams on AI, automation, or workflow transformation initiatives.

  Experience using analytics and field feedback to refine programs over time.

  Why this role matters
 This role will help shape how Ironclad’s Sales teams sell in the next chapter of the market. The opportunity is bigger than running programs. It is about helping the field operate with more confidence, more consistency, and more leverage by combining strong enablement fundamentals with practical AI adoption.
 Success in this role means the field has clearer guidance, stronger reinforcement, better AI readiness, and a more coherent enablement experience across priority moments that matter most.
  Base Salary Range: $150,000 - $170,000 +bonus +equity 
 The base salary range represents the minimum and maximum of the salary range for this position based at our San Francisco headquarters. The actual base salary offered for this position will depend on numerous factors, including individual proficiency, anticipated performance, and the location of the selected candidate. Our base salary is just one component of Ironclad’s competitive total rewards package, which also includes equity awards (a new hire grant, along with opportunities for additional awards throughout your tenure), competitive health and wellness benefits, and a commitment to career growth and development.

title: Staff Site Reliability Engineer
summary: Replit is hiring a Staff Site Reliability Engineer to improve the reliability, scalability, observability, and performance of infrastructure serving millions of developers. The role involves leading incident response, defining reliability standards, building automation and infrastructure as code, optimizing Kubernetes-based cloud deployments, debugging distributed systems, mentoring engineers, and writing production-quality Python or Go code.
description:
Replit is the agentic software creation platform that enables anyone to build applications using natural language. With millions of users worldwide, Replit is democratizing software development by removing traditional barriers to application creation.
  About the role: 
 Join our Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) team and help ensure the reliability, scalability, and performance of Replit's infrastructure that serves millions of developers worldwide. As a Staff Site Reliability Engineer, you will bridge the gap between development and operations, implementing automation and establishing best practices that enable our platform to scale efficiently while maintaining high availability.
 We are seeking Staff SREs who are passionate about building and maintaining resilient systems at scale. Your mission will be to proactively find and analyze reliability problems across our stack, then design and implement software and systems to create step-function improvements. You will design robust observability solutions, lead incident response, automate operational tasks, and continuously improve our infrastructure's reliability, all while mentoring and educating the broader engineering team to make reliability a core value at Replit.
  You Will: 
    Architect and Implement Observability:  Design, build, and lead the implementation of comprehensive monitoring, logging, and tracing solutions. Create dashboards and metrics that provide real-time visibility into system health and performance, enabling proactive issue detection.

   Define and Drive Reliability Standards:  Work with product and engineering teams to define, implement, and track Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and Service Level Indicators (SLIs). Build systems to monitor and report on these metrics, holding teams accountable and ensuring we maintain high reliability standards while balancing innovation speed.

   Lead Incident Management and Response:  Act as a senior leader during high-impact incidents, guiding the team to rapid resolution. Conduct thorough, blameless post-mortems and drive the implementation of preventative measures. Develop and refine runbooks and build automation to reduce Mean Time To Recovery (MTTR).

   Drive Automation and Infrastructure as Code:  Architect, build, and improve automation to eliminate toil and operational work. Design and maintain CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure automation using tools like Terraform or Pulumi. Create self-healing systems that can automatically respond to common failure scenarios.

   Optimize Performance on Kubernetes:  Collaborate with core infrastructure and product teams to performance-tune and optimize our large-scale cloud deployments, with a deep focus on Kubernetes, Docker, and GCP. Identify and resolve performance bottlenecks, implement capacity planning strategies, and reduce latency across global regions.

   Debug and Harden Distributed Systems:  Dive deep into debugging extremely difficult technical problems across the stack. Use your findings to design and implement long-term fixes that make our systems and products more robust, operable, and easier to diagnose.

   Provide Staff-Level Guidance:  Review feature and system designs from across the company, acting as a key owner for the reliability, scalability, security, and operational integrity of those designs.

   Educate and Mentor:  Educate, mentor, and hold accountable the broader engineering team to improve the reliability of our systems, making reliability a core value of the Replit engineering culture.

   Build and Integrate:  Write high-quality, well-tested code in Python or Go to meet the needs of your customers, whether it's building new internal tools or integrating with third-party vendors.

   Required Skills and Experience: 
   8-10 years of experience in Site Reliability Engineering or similar roles (e.g., DevOps, Systems Engineering, Infrastructure Engineering).

  Strong programming skills in languages like Python or Go. You write high-quality, well-tested code.

  Deep understanding of distributed systems. You’ve designed, built, scaled, and maintained production services and know how to compose a service-oriented architecture.

  Deep experience with container orchestration platforms, specifically  Kubernetes , and cloud-native technologies.

  Proven track record of designing, implementing, and maintaining sophisticated  monitoring and observability  solutions (e.g., metrics, logging, tracing).

  Strong  incident management  skills with extensive experience leading incident response for complex systems and demonstrated critical thinking under pressure.

  Experience with infrastructure as code (e.g., Terraform, Pulumi) and configuration management tools.

  Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with an ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly and simply and a bias toward open, transparent cultural practices.

  Strong interpersonal skills, with experience working with and mentoring engineers from junior to principal levels.

  A willingness to dive into understanding, debugging, and improving any layer of the stack.

  You're passionate about making software creation accessible and empowering the next generation of builders.

   Bonus Points: 
   Deep experience with Google Cloud Platform (GCP) services and tools.

  Expert-level knowledge of modern observability platforms (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, OpenTelemetry).

  Experience designing and building reliable systems capable of handling high throughput and low latency.

  Significant experience with Go and Terraform.

  Familiarity with working in rapid-growth, startup environments.

  Experience writing company-facing blog posts and training materials.

title: Staff Software Engineer
summary: The Staff Software Engineer leads architecture, technical direction, and delivery for Axios’ core products across multiple teams while remaining a hands-on individual contributor. Responsibilities include building and operating frontend and backend systems, improving reliability and security, applying AI-enabled engineering practices, leading cross-team initiatives, and mentoring engineers.
description:
1 big thing: Axios is a growth-focused media company helping people get smarter, faster, on what matters. We’re looking for a Staff Software Engineer—a senior, hands-on individual contributor—to lead architecture and delivery for Axios’ core products across multiple teams using strong product-engineering and AI-native practices.

Why it matters: Axios delivers clear, trustworthy news to millions of readers. You’ll be anchored to a product area while shaping full-stack systems and technical direction across multiple teams and connected systems. This is not a people-management role.

AI is core to how we build. You’ll use coding agents throughout implementation, testing, review, debugging, documentation, and operations while remaining accountable for architecture, quality, security, and product outcomes. Staff impact comes from sustained scope, judgment, and results—not tool use alone.

You’ll work with product managers, designers, engineers, and leaders to shape plans, align dependencies, resolve ambiguity, build resilient systems, and help others make better technical decisions.

Responsibilities:

As a Staff Software Engineer, you’ll lead reliable product and platform work across Axios’ frontend and backend systems. You’ll remain hands-on while driving multi-quarter initiatives, improving technical coherence, and using agentic practices to accelerate delivery. Key responsibilities include:

  • Cross-team technical leadership: Lead mission-critical or high-risk initiatives spanning teams and connected systems. Frame problems, align ownership and dependencies, make tradeoffs explicit, and drive production adoption.
  • Architecture and design: Own architecture for a product area and scalable boundaries across frontend, APIs, data, and production systems. Lead design reviews and establish standards within your sphere of influence.
  • Hands-on system ownership: Own the technical direction and long-term evolution of key systems while writing and reviewing code, prototyping, debugging, leading migrations, and operating services in production.
  • AI-enabled product and engineering: Identify where models, agents, retrieval, or automation create value. Build reusable capabilities with measurable behavior, guardrails, and judgment about when conventional software is better.
  • Quality, reliability, and incident leadership: Improve testing, performance, observability, security, and operational readiness. Anticipate systemic risks, address technical debt, and help lead resolution and learning during critical production issues.
  • Technical leadership and mentorship: Mentor mid- and senior-level engineers across teams, spread systems thinking and design patterns, and build alignment through proposals, reviews, and influence without authority.
  • Product and technical strategy: Partner with product, design, and engineering leaders to shape the product-area roadmap, align dependencies, and connect technical investment to reader, editorial, and business outcomes.

Skills:

The ideal candidate is a staff-level engineer with sustained multi-team impact, deep expertise in a relevant domain, broad systems thinking, and a commitment to user experience, reliability, scalability, maintainable code, and effective AI-enabled practice. You should have:

  • Experience: Typically 7+ years in professional software development, or equivalent sustained Staff-level impact, including leading complex initiatives across multiple teams or systems.
  • AI-native development: Hands-on experience using agentic coding tools—such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, or comparable tools—to complete meaningful, multi-step software work, rather than only generating snippets or using autocomplete.
  • Agent direction and context: Ability to write clear strategies, specifications, and acceptance criteria; provide context; scope complex work; decide what to delegate; and redirect incomplete or incorrect approaches.
  • Verification and engineering judgment: Ability to review AI-generated code critically, validate assumptions, identify security, scalability, and maintainability risks, and catch plausible but wrong solutions. You understand that AI raises the importance of sound architecture, testing, and human judgment.
  • Frontend development: Hands-on experience building production interfaces with JavaScript or TypeScript and React, preferably with Next.js, plus judgment to guide frontend architecture across teams.
  • Backend development: Hands-on experience building production services and APIs. Our backend systems use Go and Python, and you should be able to shape reliable service boundaries and work effectively in or learn either language.
  • Data fundamentals: Experience with relational databases, SQL, schema design, transactions, and migrations.
  • Quality and security: Experience with testing, accessibility, input validation, authentication, authorization, and web security practices, plus the ability to raise standards across teams.
  • Engineering judgment: Ability to operate independently in ambiguity, identify high-leverage problems, align teams, make sound tradeoffs, and connect decisions to product and business goals—including when AI is not the right tool.
  • Communication: Ability to build alignment through clear proposals and reasoning, communicate risks and tradeoffs across functions, and drive clarity during disagreement.
  • Continuous learning: Curiosity about changing models, tools, and practices, paired with an evidence-based approach. You share useful patterns, identify what fails, and make others more effective.

We’ll be even more excited if you have:

  • Experience building production AI-enabled features using model APIs, structured outputs, tool or function calling, retrieval, or agent workflows.
  • Experience evaluating and operating AI-enabled systems through regression tests, evaluation harnesses, tracing, feedback loops, model or prompt versioning, cost and latency monitoring, or human-review paths.
  • Experience extending AI development environments through MCP servers, agent tools, repository instructions, reusable skills or plugins, custom workflows, or automated code review.
  • Led a multi-team architecture, platform, migration, or modernization initiative from problem framing through production adoption.
  • Owned critical systems through incidents, scaling challenges, and long-term architectural evolution.
  • Drove adoption of technical standards, reusable tools, or platform capabilities across multiple teams.
  • Mentored experienced engineers and helped improve technical judgment beyond your immediate team.
  • Experience with CMS, publishing, media, subscription, search, or other consumer-facing products.
  • Production experience with Go or Python and distributed systems using gRPC, cloud infrastructure, containers, queues, CI/CD, or similar technologies.

What success looks like:

  • Cross-team delivery: You drive multi-quarter initiatives from problem framing through production adoption, aligning dependencies and ownership to produce durable outcomes.
  • Engineering leverage: Teams deliver more effectively because of the standards, tools, architecture, documentation, and context you create. You establish safe, repeatable AI patterns where they add value.
  • System health: Key systems become more reliable, scalable, secure, observable, and easier to change. You reduce systemic risk and improve incident prevention and response.
  • Product-area impact: Your decisions support Axios’ readers, products, editorial workflows, and business goals within the teams and systems you influence.
  • Organizational technical leadership: Engineers across teams make better decisions through your mentorship, proposals, reviews, and example. You remain a hands-on IC who multiplies others’ effectiveness.

 

Starting salary for this role is in the range of $165,000 - $215,000 and is dependent on numerous factors, including but not limited to location, work experience, and skills. This range does not include other compensation benefits. Axios' compensation philosophy takes into account the cost of labor differentials across the country. Because this is a remote-optional job posting, this salary range takes into account all possible locations within the United States, but candidates will only be eligible for the salary range for their location.

Axios is committed to embracing artificial intelligence as a core part of how we work. All team members are expected to actively develop AI literacy and use AI tools to enhance their productivity, creativity, and efficiency. We invest in ongoing learning to ensure every employee is equipped to responsibly and effectively integrate AI into their daily workflows.
