title: AI Learning Experience Designer
summary: The AI Learning Experience Designer will design, build, and improve AI-powered, simulation-based training, including role-play scenarios, procedural simulations, and adaptive learning experiences. The role bridges instructional design, facilitation, and Product/Engineering by translating learning needs into technical requirements, managing simulation tooling, measuring learning impact, and ensuring accessibility and data privacy.
description:
Company Overview:

Blink Health is the fastest growing healthcare technology company that builds products to make prescriptions accessible and affordable to everybody.  Our two primary products – BlinkRx and Quick Save – remove traditional roadblocks within the current prescription supply chain, resulting in better access to critical medications and improved health outcomes for patients. 

BlinkRx is the world’s first pharma-to-patient cloud that offers a digital concierge service for patients who are prescribed branded medications. Patients benefit from transparent low prices, free home delivery, and world-class support on this first-of-its-kind centralized platform. With BlinkRx, never again will a patient show up at the pharmacy only to discover that they can’t afford their medication, their doctor needs to fill out a form for them, or the pharmacy doesn’t have the medication in stock. 

We are a highly collaborative team of builders and operators who invent new ways of working in an industry that historically has resisted innovation. Join us!

The Role: As our AI Learning Experience Designer, you'll drive our organization's shift toward AI-powered, simulation-based training. You won't just write training content — you'll design, build, and continuously improve realistic practice environments, from conversational role-play scenarios to procedural and technical simulations, that let employees rehearse high-stakes skills safely, repeatedly, and at scale. This role sits deliberately at the intersection of three disciplines: instructional design, live facilitation, and Product/Engineering. You'll translate learning needs into technical requirements that designers or Product and Engineering can build against, and translate those outputs back into the classroom experience for our learners. Success means simulation-based training that is both instructionally sound and technically scalable — and that demonstrably improves performance.

This is a hybrid role based in either New York or Seattle location

What you’ll do:

Simulation Design & Strategy

  • Design branching scenarios, role-play conversations, and procedural/technical simulations grounded in adult learning principles and real on-the-job situations.
  • Define what “realistic” and “effective” mean for each simulation — personas, difficulty curves, failure states, and feedback loops — in partnership with SMEs and facilitators.
  • Build and maintain a simulation roadmap aligned to the organization’s highest-priority skill gaps, rather than defaulting to whichever tool is easiest to deploy.

AI Tooling, Prompt Engineering & Build

  • Own the prompt engineering and configuration behind AI-driven simulations (conversational AI role-play, AI-generated scenario content, adaptive difficulty), working within licensed platforms and/or custom-built tools.
  • Evaluate and pilot AI simulation vendors and in-house technologies (e.g., conversational role-play platforms, authoring tools with AI generation, avatar/voice tools) against defined learning outcomes and total cost of ownership.
  • Maintain a working knowledge of the AI/LLM capabilities and constraints relevant to training use cases, translating this into realistic scope and timelines.

Bridging Instructional Design, Facilitation & Product/Engineering

  • Act as the primary liaison between the L&D function and P&E teams building or supporting simulation tooling — writing clear requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria on the learning side. Serve as a product owner for L&D outcomes.
  • Partner with facilitators and trainers to pressure-test simulations before rollout, incorporating live-delivery feedback into design and technical iteration.
  • Translate technical/platform constraints (data privacy, integration limits, latency, model behavior) into design trade-offs that instructional design and facilitation stakeholders can understand and plan around.
  • Represent L&D in Product/Engineering planning processes where simulation tooling, data, or infrastructure decisions affect training outcomes.

Innovation & Process Ownership

  • Pioneer AI-driven design and production processes that let the team scale simulation output while maintaining quality — this role owns how simulations get built, not just what gets built.
  • Stay current on emerging AI tools and techniques relevant to simulation and instructional design, and make the call on when to adopt, pilot, or pass.

Measurement & Continuous Improvement

  • Define and track success metrics for each simulation (e.g., time-to-competency, skill transfer, manager/coach ratings, performance-data correlation), not just completion or satisfaction scores.
  • Use practice and performance analytics to identify where simulations are and aren’t closing real skill gaps, and iterate accordingly.
  • Report on simulation program impact to L&D leadership, tying results to business outcomes rather than production speed alone.

Governance & Quality

  • Ensure simulations meet accessibility standards (e.g., WCAG, Section 508) and organizational data privacy/security requirements for any AI tool used.
  • Establish and maintain a quality/review process for AI-generated simulation content before it reaches learners.

A successful applicant will fit the following criteria:

We want someone who lives at the intersection of learning design and technology. You’ll thrive here if:

  • You have 7+ years in instructional design, learning experience design, or a closely related L&D role.
  • You have demonstrated experience building with AI to design, develop, and scale learning experiences, including AI-assisted content generation, prompt engineering, content transformation, and workflow optimization — not just general AI familiarity.
  • You have demonstrated experience creating AI-generated learning assets, specifically simulations, chatbots, branching scenarios, role-play conversations, assessments, and coaching/reinforcement activities (a portfolio or work samples demonstrating this is required).
  • You have experience partnering directly with P&E teams or other technical partners in their planning process, and you communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • You have experience designing for and/or delivering live facilitation (virtual or in-person), or working closely with facilitators to pressure-test and shape training content before rollout.
  • You have experience translating business priorities and performance gaps into scalable learning solutions, ideally in a fast-paced or customer-facing organization.
  • You have a strong grounding in instructional design methodology (e.g., ADDIE, adult learning theory) and scenario/branching-logic design.
  • You have working proficiency with at least one AI simulation/role-play platform (e.g., Second Nature, Hyperbound, Mindtickle, Zenarate, SmartWinnr, or comparable) and one standard authoring/content tool stack (e.g., Articulate Storyline/Rise, Vyond, Claude Design) with AI-assisted features.
  • You’re familiar with the systems a Product/Engineering-adjacent L&D role needs to operate in: an LMS (e.g., Cornerstone, Absorb, Moodle), a CMS (e.g., Showpad), and a project-tracking tool used by Engineering (e.g., Jira) — enough to work inside these systems, not just consume their output.
  • You have strong project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple concurrent initiatives and competing stakeholder priorities without losing quality.
  • You’re comfortable reading and acting on learning/performance analytics — engagement, adoption, time-to-competency, and business performance data — to demonstrate program impact, not just completion.
  • You communicate clearly and technically — able to write requirements Engineering can build from and explain platform constraints to non-technical stakeholders.
  • You have an innovation-oriented mindset: you’re comfortable proposing and piloting AI-driven processes that compress traditional development timelines, and comfortable being wrong sometimes in service of moving faster.
  • You have a bachelor’s degree in Instructional Design, Learning Experience Design, Educational Technology, or a related field; equivalent professional experience will be considered in lieu of a degree.

Why Join Us:

It is rare to have a company that both deeply impacts its customers and is able to provide its services across a massive population.  At Blink, we have a huge impact on people when they are most vulnerable: at the intersection of their healthcare and finances. We are also the fastest growing healthcare company in the country and are driving that impact across millions of new patients every year.  Our business model not only helps people, but drives economics that allow us to build a generational company. We are a relentlessly learning, constantly curious, and aggressively collaborative cross-functional team dedicated to inventing new ways to improve the lives of our customers.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity of all kinds. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

Applicants who provide their phone number and consent to receive text messages may receive SMS or MMS updates from Blink Health regarding their application.

title: Regional Vice President of AI Enablement & Implementation
summary: The Regional Vice President of AI Enablement & Implementation will establish and execute AI roadmaps for a portfolio of Crescent-managed hotels, identifying high-impact opportunities and leading solutions from evaluation through implementation, adoption, measurement, and optimization. The role partners with hotel operators and cross-functional teams to apply AI, automation, data, and process redesign to business challenges and deliver measurable operational and financial outcomes.
description:
Help Shape What AI Looks Like in Hospitality. 
  AI is changing how businesses operate. At Crescent Hotels & Resorts, we’re focused on something bigger than simply adopting new technology—we want to put AI to work solving real business problems across our hotels. 
 We are seeking a Regional Vice President of AI Enablement & Implementation   to help turn that vision into reality. 
  This is an opportunity for a builder. 
  You’ll work alongside Crescent leaders, hotel operators, ownership partners, and functional experts to identify where AI can create meaningful value—and then help take those ideas from   opportunity to solution to implementation to measurable results.
  We aren’t looking for someone to simply tell us what AI    could    do. 
  We’re looking for someone who can help us   make it happen.
  What You’ll Build 
  Imagine helping create AI-enabled solutions that could: 
   Give a General Manager a daily    “GM Pulse”    that brings together revenue, labor, cost, guest satisfaction, and operational signals into one actionable briefing. 
  Help a sales team qualify an inbound RFP and develop a tailored group proposal in a fraction of the time. 
  Optimize hotel labor schedules against forecasted demand to reduce overtime, overstaffing, and unnecessary contract labor. 
  Automate repetitive accounting processes, reconciliations, cash-flow forecasting, and reporting. 
  Monitor F&B inventory and purchasing patterns to identify waste and over-ordering. 
  Help recruiting teams source, screen, schedule, and communicate with candidates more efficiently. 
  Turn financial, STR, guest satisfaction, revenue, and operating data into recurring ownership and investor reporting. 
  Make it easier for hotel associates and leaders to find information, make decisions, and spend less time on administrative work. 
   And those are just the opportunities we see today. 
  A major part of your role will be helping us discover    what we haven’t thought of yet.  
  What You’ll Do 
  You’ll help establish and execute the AI roadmap for a designated portfolio of Crescent-managed hotels, identifying the opportunities with the greatest potential business impact. 
  You’ll work across    Operations, Commercial, Revenue Management, Sales, Marketing, Finance, Human Resources, and Technology    to understand how work gets done today—and where AI, automation, data, or process redesign can make it better. 
  You’ll help determine whether the right solution should be    built, bought, configured, or integrated   , and you’ll lead initiatives beyond the idea stage through implementation, adoption, measurement, and optimization. 
  You’ll partner closely with Crescent’s technology teams around systems, integrations, data, security, and governance while helping operators translate business challenges into practical AI-enabled solutions. 
  Most importantly, you’ll make sure the solutions we introduce actually get used. 
  Because successful AI transformation isn’t measured by how many pilots we launch. 
   It’s measured by what changes because of them.  
  Who We’re Looking For 
  You understand AI—but you think like a business leader. 
  You naturally start with: 
   “What problem are we trying to solve?”  
  Then you determine whether AI, automation, data, process redesign—or some combination—is the right answer. 
  You’re comfortable discussing strategy with executives one moment and sitting with an operator to understand a manual process the next. 
  You understand technologies such as    generative AI, AI agents, workflow automation, APIs, data integration, and emerging AI platforms   , but you don’t believe technology is the objective. 
   Business impact is.  
  You know how to build a business case, evaluate technology and vendors, lead cross-functional implementation, drive organizational adoption, and measure ROI. 
  Hospitality experience would be valuable, but we’re also interested in leaders who have successfully driven AI or digital transformation in other complex, multi-unit businesses. 
  What Success Looks Like 
  Your work should ultimately help Crescent and our hotels achieve measurable outcomes: 
   More revenue. 
 Better productivity. 
 Smarter labor deployment. 
 Faster decision-making. 
 Less administrative work. 
 Better guest experiences. 
 More empowered associates. 
 And demonstrable ROI from AI investments.  
  Why Crescent? 
  At    Crescent Hotels & Resorts   , hospitality is a people business—and we believe technology should make our people better at what they do, not take away from the human experience that defines great hospitality. 
  This role offers the opportunity to help shape our approach to AI at an important moment in its evolution. 
  You won’t be stepping into a mature AI program and maintaining someone else’s roadmap. 
   You’ll help build it.  
  If you are energized by the opportunity to turn emerging technology into practical solutions, challenge how work gets done, and help shape the future of AI in hospitality, we’d like to hear from you.

description:

The additional years used in place of the degree are on top of the 5 year experience requirement above, not counted within it.

title: Senior AI Learning Designer, Rapid Content
summary: WRITER is seeking a senior AI learning designer to create and ship short, targeted video-based courses on software, workflows, role-specific skills, tools, and timely AI topics. The role owns the full course lifecycle, delivers live and virtual training, repurposes content across formats, and balances proactive learning needs with rapid incoming requests. It also involves collaborating with product, marketing, customer-facing teams, and subject-matter experts while serving as the voiceover or on-camera instructor.
description:
🚀 About WRITER 
 WRITER is where the world's leading enterprises orchestrate AI-powered work. Our vision is to expand human capacity through superintelligence. And we're proving it's possible – through powerful, trustworthy AI that unites IT and business teams together to unlock enterprise-wide transformation. With WRITER's end-to-end platform, hundreds of companies like Mars, Marriott, Uber, and Vanguard are building and deploying AI agents that are grounded in their company's data and fueled by WRITER's enterprise-grade LLMs. Valued at $1.9B and backed by industry-leading investors including Premji Invest, Radical Ventures, and ICONIQ Growth, WRITER is rapidly cementing its position as the leader in enterprise generative AI.
 Founded in 2020 with office hubs in San Francisco, New York City, Seattle, Austin, Chicago, and London, our team thinks big and moves fast, and we're looking for smart, hardworking builders and scalers to join us on our journey to create a better future of work with AI.
  📐 About the role 
 In an AI-native environment, the product shifts fast, new workflows emerge weekly, and customers and internal teams surface needs in real time. Someone has to meet those needs at the speed they arise. That's this role.
 As a lead learning experience designer, you'll own a fast-paced, high-volume learning design track focused on short, targeted, just-in-time courses — typically 15–45 minutes each, built in sprints of three weeks or less, shipping roughly 15+ courses per year. You'll build focused one-off courses that plug specific gaps: a new workflow, a role-specific skill, a tool that just shipped, an AI topic that can't wait for the next curriculum cycle.
 These courses are standalone, purpose-built, and often shorter-lived — responding to the moment. You'll work both proactively (scanning for emerging needs) and reactively (fielding requests from across the company and from customers). The pace is fast, the iteration cycles are tight, and the environment is dynamic. If you're energized by change, comfortable shipping at speed, and able to balance strategic proactivity with rapid reactive response, this is your role.
 In addition, you'll deliver live and virtual trainings on these topics as needed — bringing the same speed and adaptability from your on-demand work into the live environment, whether in person or on a webinar platform.
 The primary medium for this role is video-based learning. You'll be the voice and face of your own instruction — recording voiceover or appearing on camera to teach software and AI topics, combined with screencaptures, screen recordings, and graphics. This is not a role where you'll hand off to a video team or rely on AI-generated voice. You are the teacher, and your voice is part of the craft.
 This role complements our end-to-end learning experience designers, who own robust, polished curricula built over longer timelines. You're not integrated within those larger curriculum builds; you're filling the space they can't reach. Your courses are shorter, faster, and more targeted, designed to serve a specific need and plug a gap where the larger curriculum moves too slowly. Think of it as the agile track of the LXD team: smaller scope, faster cadence, and a bias toward shipping. You won't be building three- to four-hour flagship programs. You'll be building tight, high-impact courses that get someone up to speed on a specific thing, quickly, and then moving on to the next one.
  🦸🏻‍♀️ What you'll do 
   Design and build focused, standalone courses — typically 15–45 minutes — in sprints of three weeks or less, shipping roughly 15 courses per year across topics that are specific and targeted: particular workflows, role-based skills, individual tools, and timely AI topics that demand a fast response

  Own the full design lifecycle for each course at speed — needs analysis, design, build, QA, and publish — without the extended timelines of end-to-end curriculum work, making smart scope decisions about what's essential, what can be cut, and how to deliver maximum learning value in a compact format

  Deliver live and virtual training on the topics you build, with excellence — adapting on the fly to audience questions, skill levels, and industry-specific workflows, particularly across WRITER's verticals

  Repurpose content across delivery modes (on-demand to live, live to on-demand, micro to full) maximizing reach without rebuilding from scratch

  Scan proactively for emerging learning needs by monitoring product changes, customer signals, and internal feedback, and get ahead of them before they're formally requested, while also fielding and triaging incoming requests from across the company and from customers, responding quickly with targeted courses that address real, surfaced needs

  Balance proactive and reactive work, making judgment calls about what's worth building, what can wait, and what should be deferred or declined, and ship at a cadence that keeps pace with the product and the business, prioritizing speed and relevance over exhaustive perfection

  Partner with product, product marketing, customer-facing teams, and SMEs to gather what you need quickly and keep courses moving, coordinate with end-to-end learning experience designers to avoid duplication and ensure your rapid-response courses complement rather than compete with larger curriculum, flag topics that outgrow the rapid-response format, and share insights from the fast track to inform the team's longer-term roadmap

  Deep experience creating video-based instructional content where you serve as the voiceover or on-camera talent for your own teaching. You do not rely on AI-generated voice for your training content.

   ⭐️ What you need 
   5+ years of experience in instructional design, learning experience design, or a related field, with demonstrated experience designing and shipping courses at a fast pace

  Proven ability to design effective learning in compact formats — you know how to scope tight, cut ruthlessly, and deliver high-impact learning in 15–45 minutes rather than three to four hours

  Comfort with rapid development cycles and short sprints; you've worked in fast-paced environments and you thrive there rather than burning out, embracing the pace of an AI-native environment where the topics you're building for may shift mid-sprint — and adapting without losing momentum

  Strong prioritization and triage skills — you can juggle proactive and reactive work, make tradeoffs, and say no when something doesn't warrant a course

  Excellent live facilitation skills — you're confident and effective delivering in person and virtually, able to read a room (physical or virtual), adapt on the fly, and keep learners engaged, and you're as comfortable in front of an audience as you are behind a slide deck

  Excellent stakeholder management — you can gather what you need from SMEs and partners quickly, keep things moving, and communicate clearly about expectations, with proficiency in standard LXD tools including authoring tools (e.g., Parta), LMS platforms (e.g., Skilljar), slide/presentation tools, video production tools, and basic design tools

  A portfolio that demonstrates your craft — At least 2 video-based course excerpts where you serve as the voiceover or on-camera talent for your own teaching — combining your own voice with screencaptures, screen recordings, and graphics to teach software or AI topics. Static text- and graphics-based samples alone don't demonstrate what this role requires. This is a chance to show us the full breadth of what you can do — video, graphics, interactive elements, slide design, in-product walkthroughs, or any combination — but video-based teaching with your own voice should be central.

  
 🍩 Benefits & perks (US Full-time employees) 
   Generous PTO, plus company holidays

  Medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your family

  Paid parental leave for all parents (16 weeks)

  Fertility and family planning support

  Early-detection cancer testing   through Galleri  

  Flexible spending account and dependent FSA options

  Health savings account for eligible plans with company contribution

  Annual work-life stipends for:
   Wellness stipend for gym, massage/chiropractor, personal training, etc.

  Learning and development stipend

 
  Company-wide off-sites and team off-sites

  Competitive compensation, company stock options and 401k

   WRITER is an equal-opportunity employer and is committed to diversity. We don't make hiring or employment decisions based on race, color, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, sex, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other basis protected by applicable local, state or federal law. Under the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. 
 By submitting your application on the application page, you acknowledge and agree to  WRITER's Global Candidate Privacy Notice .

title: Content Strategist (remote Us) - Future Opening
summary: The Content Strategist develops and manages custom content and SEO strategies for enterprise B2B technology and SaaS clients. Responsibilities include client deliverables, goal setting and reporting, project management, content campaign development, stakeholder communication, and identifying account growth opportunities.
description:
Directive Consulting is the leading B2B marketing agency for brands that are serious about the metrics that matter most.
 
With over a decade of expertise and 420+ B2B brands under our belt, we've earned our reputation on real outcomes. We run through 3 divisions: Performance, Communications, and Commerce, all wired to share intelligence and answer to revenue. That system spans everything from Paid Media and Content Marketing, to PR and Paid Social, to Marketplace and Lifecycle Marketing. Tying it all together is our methodology, DiscoverabilityOS™, which aligns brand and demand to guide your ICP to choose you across every decision point.

We move fast. We think boldly. We hire people who challenge the status quo, build campaigns worth talking about, and make bold brands impossible to ignore. If you live for performance, love solving hard problems, and want your work to actually mean something, you'll fit right in.
  At Directive, we’re always looking ahead to connect with talented professionals who excel at crafting strategies that elevate search visibility, developing compelling content, and delivering value to audiences. 
  As we continue to grow, we’re always seeking forward-thinking individuals who thrive in fast-paced environments, are obsessed with analytics and storytelling, and are eager to make their mark in B2B tech and SaaS marketing. 
  If you're ready to explore future opportunities and be part of a team that values creativity, strategy, and results, we’d love to connect with you!! 

 About The Role: 
 The Content Strategist is a crucial, client-facing role that is responsible for day-to-day client deliverables, creating and managing custom client strategies, and communicating both with clients and internal stakeholders. The Strategist is responsible for more Enterprise clients and is expected to have a deep understanding of their service line and how it impacts other areas of business to create a holistic marketing strategy.
  Please note: internally, this role is titled Account Strategist, Content & SEO. 
  What You'll Do: 
    Strategic Excellence and Best Practices:  Strategists are responsible for creating custom strategies and implementing best practices for their clients that ultimately result in achieving our NSMs. The strategist will use project phase as a foundational moment for building the initial client strategy, but will also use our clients overall marketing goals, current and ongoing campaigns, and historical performance to optimize and revise strategies over the lifetime of the client while adhering to Directive best practices
   Strategists will work closely with their Associate Director (AsD) when roadblocks arise that impact their strategy and goal attainment.

  Strategists display a strong ability to craft creative briefs and compelling content campaigns with a focus on ideation based on competitor and audience insights.

  Best practices should be used to inform our strategies to ensure our clients are in the best position to exceed their goals. In particular:
   LTV:CAC modeling

  Customer Generation

  Share of SERP

  Content Production

 
 
   Goal Setting:  Strategists are responsible for using available data to set goals for clients during their engagement period. These goals will be reviewed and approved by their Associate Director (AsD), who should be in the meeting with them.
   Data sources include Google Analytics, CRM data, SEMRush reporting, and Ahrefs reporting

  All Goals must be approved by the Associate Director (AsD) before the Strategist can present it to their client alongside their Associate Director (AsD).

 
   Project Management:  Strategists are responsible for ensuring that their planned strategy is executed. Project Management ensures that the Directive team and the client team knows who is responsible for specific tasks to ensure we make progress towards our goals.
   Use of the project management tool Asana is required.

  This includes delegating tasks to other team members, such as Specialists, as well as our clients and then ensuring that these tasks are completed in a timely manner.

  In pods where Project Managers are present, Strategists will ensure they partner with Project Managers to ensure all tasks are created, assigned and due dates are met and communicated to the client

  Strategists will work closely with content writers and designers to complete content campaigns for clients on time while also being responsible for ensuring that the quality is up to client standards.

 
   Internal and External Communication:  Strategists are the main interface between our clients and our team. Strategists are expected to build relationships with our clients that goes beyond just deliverables and get to know them on a human level with the primary goal of being the best consultant for our clients and their business. Additionally Strategists are expected to proactively communicate to clients and internal leadership on a regular basis to ensure we are driving the best results for clients.
   When proactively communicating with clients we want to ensure we communicate timeline expectations for deliverables, goal attainment progress, and actively use our shared communication channels, such as Slack, to communicate between bi-weekly meetings. This includes sending deliverables on a regular cadence instead of only during bi-weekly meetings

  When proactively communicating with internal leadership this should include communicating any roadblocks, opportunities for account growth, and any moments of change on clients accounts. Moments of change can look like a needed change in strategy, internal client marketing changes, point of contact changes, and more.

 
   Reporting:  Strategists are expected to regularly report to clients the progress and impact of their strategy. In support of this pilar strategists are expected to report on the following cadence:
   Bi-weekly meetings with the client
   Note in these meetings strategists are expected to report on NSM progress and ongoing deliverables

 
  Monthly reports

  Quarterly reports

  2 Bi-Annual business review presentation

 
   What You'll Bring: 
   A proven track record of success around implementing SEO principles and content strategy: keyword research, on-page optimization, and link building

  Analytical insight: ability to analyse website traffic and SEO metrics using tools like Google Analytics

  Strong Communication skills: comfortable client facing and owning relationships with key stakeholders

  Strong familiarity with industry tools such as Google Search Console, Google Analytics, SEMRush, Ahrefs, Screaming Frog/crawling tools

  Proven organisational, project, and time management skills

  Genuine enthusiasm for digital marketing, SEO and Content

  Must have agency experience

  Must have B2B tech and/or SaaS experience

  Driven to stay ahead of industry trends, including actively learning how AI and automation can enhance marketing and operations.

   Goals: 
   NSM Attainment: 100%

  MRR Retainment: 96%

  CSAT > 4.2

  Upsells / Cross-sells / Referrals -
   Strategists are expected to regularly look for opportunities for our clients to grow their business with Directive.
   Examples of this include:
   Growing into another service line such as SEO or Paid Media

  Growing within their current service line such as increasing content, SEO, or Paid Media budgets

 
 
  Referrals are a natural extension of building a solid relationship with our clients and strategists should be in the habit of asking for a referral at key moments.
   Example of moments to ask for a referral:
   Point of contact starts a new job

 
 
  Client leaves a 5 CSAT score

 
   What We Offer 
 🏠 Compensation for this role includes a competitive base salary in the $75,000-95,000 USD range, commensurate with experience and geography.
 🙏 Medical, dental, vision plans, disability, and life insurance coverage for you and your family that fit your lifestyle
 Including a 100% employer-paid plan for you and a 50% employer contribution for your dependents
 Benefits to Support the Whole Person:
 🧠 Mental - Access to certified therapists through Spring Health, membership to Headspace
 💪 Physical - Gympass
 🛫 Time Off - Unlimited PTO (2-week minimum), Paid Company Holidays, Your Birthday Off, End of Year Recharge (Closed December 24 - January 1), Paid Parental Leave
 💰 Financial - Traditional and Roth 401(k) with a 3% company match
 🌟 Bonus - Annual bonus based on tenure, which scales in total amount over time
 🌴 Annual Anniversary Trip with peers and executive leadership for fun and entertainment!
  Work Environment Requirements 
 As a remote-first company, you’ll have the ability to work from your home office. For some positions, as posted, we will accommodate global opportunities where we have established businesses, including Canada, Mexico, and the UK. For global locations, you must have established and current work authorization and permanently reside in that country.
 This role has the opportunity to operate 100% virtually from your home office. We primarily collaborate with our colleagues through virtual meetings (Zoom), and Slack. In this role, you will be required to operate a laptop computer (PC or Mac available), computer software platforms, and other office productivity tools as necessary. Due to the nature of this role, you must be able to remain stationary for extended periods, must be able to observe and interpret written and/or verbal communication, must have reliable internet access, and a professional background.
 To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential job duty satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform essential job functions.
 If you require reasonable accommodations in completing this application, interviewing, completing any pre-employment testing, or otherwise participating in the employee selection process, direct your inquiries to recruiting@directiveconsulting.com.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

description:

  Position Summary and Responsibilities : Working from your home and at monthly in-person sites across Maine, certified teachers will utilize the Pearson Online Classroom to support and motivate students in working through their curriculum, deliver synchronous instruction, provide intervention and enrichment, and use data to diagnose student learning needs. The Secondary English Teacher will be responsible for the successful completion of the following tasks:

  Deliver engaging English/Language Arts instruction via asynchronous recordings, synchronous LiveLessons, and individualized support sessions.
 Write and maintain lesson plans that align with curriculum standards and ensure content is rigorous, accessible, and relevant.
 Provide differentiated instruction and resources to meet diverse learner needs, including those outlined in IEPs and 504 Plans.

  Compliance & Administration 
  Ensure accurate recordkeeping of attendance, communication logs, student progress, and compliance with IEP/504 accommodations.
 Participate in the training, organization, and administration of state and other required assessments.
 Support school-wide recruiting and marketing efforts by representing the school as needed.
 Uphold a commitment to equitable and inclusive practices in all aspects of the role.
 Other duties as assigned.
 
  Requirements: 
  Certified to teach Secondary English in Maine
 Strong technology skills (especially with Microsoft Office products and Google Suite)
 Excellent communication skills, both oral and written
 Highly organized and punctual
 Student and family-focused approach
 High degree of flexibility
 Demonstrated ability to work well in a fast-paced environment
 Team player track record
 Strong interpersonal skills which include the ability to work effectively with students, parents, staff, and community members from diverse backgrounds.
 Willingness to travel for marketing and state testing events (may require occasional overnight travel)

description:

title: Instructional Designer - Full Time - Higher ED
summary: The Instructional Designer develops and maintains instructional materials and courses for online, hybrid, and face-to-face healthcare programs in higher education. Responsibilities include designing LMS-based courses, creating multimedia and eLearning content, collaborating with subject matter experts, ensuring accessibility and compliance, evaluating learning technologies, and supporting continuous course improvement.
description:
Company Description
 Unitek Learning is a leading healthcare education organization focused on preparing the next generation of nurses and healthcare professionals. 
 Through its family of institutions, including Unitek College of Nursing, Eagle Gate College, Provo College, Brookline College, and Unitek EMT, Unitek delivers career-focused education designed to help students build meaningful careers while addressing critical workforce needs across the healthcare industry. 
 Through our Workforce Solutions segment, Unitek partners with hospitals and health systems to create sustainable talent pipelines and expand access to healthcare education through employer-based training and workforce development programs nationwide.
 Job Description
 The Instructional Designer creates, develops, and maintains instructional materials to support online, hybrid, and face-to-face delivery of healthcare courses in higher education. This role ensures course quality, alignment with learning outcomes, and effective use of instructional technologies. The position also supports faculty and academic teams by applying instructional design best practices and facilitating continuous improvement in course delivery.
  Design and develop courses within the institution’s Learning Management System (LMS) to ensure high-quality student learning experience.
 Create engaging instructional content including course overviews, syllabi, learning outcomes, multimedia activities, and assessments.
 Build and publish eLearning modules that integrate interactive elements and align with course outcomes.
 Collaborate closely with subject matter experts (SMEs) to translate technical or specialized knowledge into engaging, student-centered learning experiences. Guide SMEs in applying instructional best practices, align content with program outcomes, and ensure materials are accurate, accessible, and pedagogically sound.
 Apply evidence-based instructional strategies grounded in adult learning theory and best practices for higher education.
 Ensure curriculum alignment by participating in committee meetings and integrating approved updates into course design.
 Review and revise instructional materials to maintain accuracy, accessibility, and compliance with institutional and regulatory standards.
 Document and maintain course resources while contributing to shared training and knowledgebase materials.
 Pilot and evaluate new learning technologies and recommend appropriate tools for adoption.
 Stay current with instructional design trends and apply knowledge of accessibility, copyright, and compliance requirements.
 Support continuous improvement by gathering feedback, analyzing outcomes, and suggesting course enhancements.
 Perform other duties as assigned.
  *Please note that this position is hybrid at our Tempe Corporate Office
 Qualifications
  Master’s degree in instructional design, instructional technology, or related field.
 Minimum of 2 years’ experience designing and delivering higher education courses.
 Proficiency with instructional technology and multimedia authoring tools.
 Strong knowledge of learning theories and instructional design models.
 Experience with course development software and LMS (Canvas experience preferred).
 Excellent writing and editing skills for instructional content.
 Strong project management and organizational skills.
 Ability to collaborate with diverse stakeholders, provide excellent customer service, and adapt to new technologies.
 Knowledge of regulatory and compliance requirements for online learning (e.g., FERPA, copyright, ADA).
 Experience applying learning theory to develop online courses (4+ years preferred).
 Higher education administration experience a plus.

 2 Weeks’ starting Vacation per year.  Increasing based on years of service with company
 12 paid Holidays and 2 Floating Holiday
 401K with a Company Match
 Company Paid Life Insurance at 1x’s your annual salary
 Leadership development and training for career advancement
 Tuition assistance and Forgiveness for you and your family up to 100% depending on program

summary: McKesson is seeking an Instructional Designer to create and maintain curriculum, e-learning, training programs, assessments, and multimedia learning materials for customer experience and supply chain operations. The role manages the instructional design lifecycle, partners with subject matter experts and stakeholders, conducts train-the-trainer sessions, maintains LMS content, and evaluates learning effectiveness.
description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.
 What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.
 Title: Instructional Designer 
 Location: Fort Worth, TX; Memphis, TN; Olive Branch, MS; Conroe, TX; Lakeland, FL 
  Onsite/Hybrid/Remote:  HYBRID role / 1 day per month onsite 
 Design Portfolio: Yes (REQUIRED) 
 *Please include a link to your design portfolio on your resume for consideration.
 The Instructional Designer is a member of the Learning Development and Delivery team within the Pharma organization designing and developing curriculum for the Customer Experience Operations and Supply Chain Operations organizations. The subject matter may include content for the various groups including Customer and Technical Solutions, Shared Services and Distribution Centers for both new hire training and existing employee development. This position reports to Supervisor, Training Content Development for Supply Chain Operations.
 Primarily, the role of Instructional Designer functions as the department subject matter expert (SME) for instructional design, e-Learning, and learning technologies demonstrating up-to-date expertise in adult learning theory, best practices, various delivery modalities, and innovative technologies.
  Key responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 
   Manage Subject Matter Experts (SME's) and stakeholder relationships to clearly understand the business, target audience and content needs to construct learning and performance outcomes.

  Develop content using various learning technology tools and resources.

  Analyze, build, develop, and maintain new hire training program(s).

  Perform business and performance analysis to determine training objectives, goals, and learner characteristics such as existing knowledge and skill level, as well as knowledge and skill gaps.

  Use knowledge of instructional system design (ISD), technologies, and adult learning theory to propose learning solutions that are cost-effective, easy-to-create and maintain, visually and instructionally compelling and that provide a rewarding experience for the learner.

  Establish goals and learning objectives to design appropriate and effective curriculum by leveraging instructional design methodology.

  Manage the end-to-end instructional design process with a sense of urgency and a drive for results.

  Employ a rapid-development approach and strong instructional design to build creative and innovative training videos, games, job aids, posters, manuals, and related learning/e-learning deliverables. Bring best-of-breed learning techniques and technology into the development of training programs and solutions.

  Conduct train-the-trainer sessions (both virtual and instructor led) to ensure delivery of materials is consistent across all markets and trainers understand the course content, learning objectives, delivery method, and evaluation procedures.

  Ensure smooth transition from final material design to implementation of program by partnering with the delivery team.

  Drive projects to successfully execute, manage project milestones, and team responsibilities for accountability.

  Manage and maintain content, enroll/assign learning objects, and run various reports using the LMS.

  Design course-level assessments to ensure learning objectives were addressed in the content at an appropriate learning level. Analyze for effectiveness.

   Compile and analyze dashboard results on evaluations (assessing readiness, job, and business impact).

  Other training responsibilities as defined by leadership and the organization.

   Expected Outcomes 
   Design course-level assessments to ensure learning objectives were addressed in the content at an appropriate learning level by compiling and analyzing results of evaluations (assessing readiness, job impact, and business impact).

   Minimum Requirement 
 Degree or equivalent and typically requires 2+ years of relevant experience.
  Education 
 4- year degree in related field, or equivalent experience.
  Critical Skills 
   2+ years of previous experience in instructional design and e-Learning development or related functional experience.

  Prioritization and planning skills, with demonstrated success producing high-quality deliverables on time and within budget.

  Must be detail-oriented, flexible, and can work in a fast-paced environment with multiple deadlines and shifting priorities.

  Proven success at establishing rapport with business partners at multiple levels, working on larger teams, and collaborative work habits.

  Ability to design and develop engaging and interactive training using a variety of modalities and methods.

  Advanced Microsoft Office application skills.

  Experience using authoring tools such as (Articulate Storyline/ Rise360).

  Strong written and verbal communication skills, including  proofreading/editing. 

  Proficiency with multimedia and e-learning tools such as HeyGen, PowerPoint, Vyond, Camtasia, Articulate Pro, and Storyline.

  Utilizes AI tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Articulate AI, Synthesia, Vyond AI, Canva AI, Adobe Firefly, ElevenLabs, and DALL·E) to create engaging, personalized learning content that improves learner engagement, knowledge retention, and performance.

  Graphic Design and audio/video editing experience

  Working knowledge of Learning Management Systems (Cornerstone OnDemand preferred).

   Working Conditions 
 Environment (Office, warehouse, etc.) – Office in Fort Worth, TX
 Physical Requirements (Lifting, standing, etc.) – General Office Demands

description:
Position Overview We are seeking a Project Manager to coordinate and manage the delivery, verification, tracking, and closeout of operational procedures supporting data center construction, expansion, retrofit, and infrastructure projects.
 The Project Manager will coordinate cross-functional stakeholders, manage project timelines and deliverables, monitor workflow progress, facilitate meetings, maintain project documentation, and support timely resolution of project risks and operational blockers.
 Key Responsibilities
 Project Initiation and Planning
  Review and triage incoming procedure delivery requests for new construction, expansion, and retrofit projects.
 Coordinate site discovery activities and establish project tracking requirements.
 Initiate project plans, trackers, and required project documentation.
 Distribute and manage equipment and information questionnaires.
 Coordinate introductory process-alignment sessions with facility operations stakeholders.
  Project Execution and Stakeholder Coordination
  Schedule and facilitate project kickoff meetings with facility representatives and subject matter experts (SMEs).
 Coordinate recurring operational meetings to monitor procedure verification and project progress.
 Assign and track review activities across appropriate technical or operational SMEs.
 Maintain clear communication regarding project milestones, deliverables, dependencies, and outstanding actions.
 Coordinate information flow among project stakeholders to support timely completion of deliverables.
  Project Tracking, Risk Management, and Governance
  Monitor project schedules, milestones, deliverables, and completion status.
 Maintain project trackers and provide accurate status updates.
 Monitor applicable Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and identify potential schedule or delivery risks.
 Document project issues, dependencies, and blockers.
 Escalate unresolved project issues through established management and governance processes.
 Support project reporting and operational dashboards with accurate and timely information.
  Workflow and Tracking Systems
  Manage project workflow activities using applicable ticketing and task-management systems.
 Administer workflow automation processes used for procedure delivery tracking.
 Create and maintain child tracking items and route assigned verification activities to appropriate SMEs.
 Maintain accurate task status, ownership, dependencies, and completion information.
 Experience with Buganizer or similar workflow/ticketing platforms is beneficial.
  Project Closeout
  Coordinate completion of project closeout activities and checklists.
 Track final procedure verification and required approvals/sign-offs.
 Confirm completion of outstanding project deliverables.
 Facilitate final project closeout and retrospective meetings with relevant stakeholders.
 Maintain final project documentation and status records.
  Key Deliverables
  Site-specific procedure delivery plans and project artifacts.
 Procedure verification trackers showing completion status across applicable operational disciplines.
 Project status reports and milestone tracking.
 Verification and completion metrics.
 Project health and risk updates.
 Accurate records within project tracking and workflow systems.
 Completed project closeout documentation.
  Required Qualifications
  Minimum 3 years of experience in project management, program coordination, technical operations, technical documentation, infrastructure projects, or a related professional area.
 Experience coordinating projects involving multiple stakeholders or functional teams.
 Experience managing project schedules, milestones, deliverables, risks, and dependencies.
 Experience using project management, ticketing, workflow, or task-management systems.
 Ability to organize and prioritize multiple concurrent project activities.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills.
 Ability to facilitate meetings, document action items, and follow up on assigned deliverables.
 Ability to identify project risks, blockers, and dependencies and escalate them through established processes.
 Ability to work onsite at the designated Lenoir, North Carolina data center location as required by the hybrid work arrangement.
  Preferred Qualifications
  Experience supporting data center operations, technical facilities, infrastructure engineering, construction/retrofit projects, or technical procedure/documentation programs.
 Experience working with operational or technical SMEs.
 Experience with Agile, operational workflow, or structured project-tracking processes.
 Familiarity with Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and operational performance tracking.
 Experience with Buganizer or comparable issue/task management platforms.
 Experience coordinating procedure verification or technical documentation workflows.

title: Staff (technical) Writer & Editor
summary: FAR.AI seeks a Staff Writer & Editor to lead written content across research communications, policy materials, website content, newsletters, op-eds, and position papers. The role partners with researchers, technical teams, organizational leaders, and communications staff to translate complex AI safety research into clear, accurate, and actionable messaging for technical and non-technical audiences.
description:
About Us
  FAR.AI  is a non-profit AI research institute working to ensure advanced AI is safe and beneficial for everyone. Our mission is to facilitate breakthrough AI safety research, advance global understanding of AI risks and solutions, and foster a coordinated global response.
 We’re structured to support that work from early research through real-world adoption:
  Independent by design.  We can pursue what's most impactful based on our theory of change and share what we find publicly.
  A portfolio approach.  Rather than focus on one single direction, we run diverse bets across the safety stack. We take promising ideas from initial experiments to deployment, informed by red-team partnerships with frontier labs and governments.
  Serious infrastructure for ambitious research . A dedicated engineering team runs our compute cluster and experiment-scaling stack, so researchers spend their time on research instead of on infra.
  Setting the standard . Our events convene key decision makers; our red-team works with frontier developers and governments; and our communications inform the public. Together, this drives adoption and sets the new standard in safety.
 Since our founding in July 2022, we've grown to   50+ staff  , published   40+ academic papers  , and convened leading   AI safety events  . Our work is recognized globally, with publications at premier venues such as NeurIPS, ICML including a   Best Paper Honorable Mention in 2026  , and ICLR, and features in the   Financial Times  ,   Nature News  ,   Wired Magazine   and   MIT Technology Review  . We conduct pre-deployment testing on behalf of frontier developers such as OpenAI and independent evaluations for governments   including the EU AI Office   and publish the   AI Security Leaderboard   based on our red-teaming expertise. We help steer and grow the AI safety field through   developing     research     roadmaps   with renowned researchers such as Yoshua Bengio; running   FAR.Labs  , an AI safety-focused co-working space in Berkeley housing 40+ members; and supporting the community through   targeted grants   to technical researchers.
  FAR.AI  is seeking an experienced writer and editor to lead development of our written content. You will report into our Communications Team Lead and work across the communications team to shape our narrative, content and messaging. You will work closely with our researchers to translate their research findings into actionable insights for policymakers and corporate decisionmakers across formats from op-eds, blog posts and research papers. We’d love to hear from you if you thrive on communicating complicated technical subject matters and want to shape the future of AI development toward a safer trajectory.
 About Communications at  FAR.AI 
 We believe that AI will be the defining technology of the 21st century. These systems could bring with them unprecedented benefits, but they also pose unprecedented risks, up to human extinction. We already know that AI will fundamentally affect everyone’s lives, reshaping the nature of work and upending geopolitics. Yet few people outside of Silicon Valley appreciate what is about to happen. Key decisionmakers in governments and companies have a limited view on what is to come, while the general public are even more in the dark.
 Communications at   FAR.AI   fills this urgent gap. As a research and education non-profit, we are a trusted, independent third-party that can cut through the hype, avoid fear mongering, while delivering credible warnings when a technology truly poses a danger. Our   Communications Team   partners directly with   FAR.AI   researchers to translate our work into compelling narratives that connect with our target audiences, whether policymakers, corporate decisionmakers or the general public.
 The team consists of experts in design, digital media, and media relations, ensuring our research and events reach their key audiences across various channels. Communications works with key   FAR.AI   team members, including our CEO Adam Gleave, building and amplifying their public profiles and thought leadership. Communications is deeply embedded across   FAR.AI  , partnering cross-functionally to deliver strategic projects. The team develops and executes communication plans for our key initiatives, such as our   leaderboard on AI model security   to enable consumers and policymakers to make informed decisions on their use and governance of this technology.
 About the role
  FAR.AI  is seeking a Staff Writer & Editor to own development of our written content. You will work with our researchers and red-team on pre-publication findings to write reports read by key policymakers and decisionmakers at frontier labs; develop content for public-facing products such as our   security leaderboard  ; and work with our CEO and key technical leaders to write   op-eds   and position papers that shape the field. You will craft a compelling org-wide narrative and ensure  FAR.AI ’s voice remains trusted and authoritative in the field. This is a rare opportunity to join a fast-growing, mission-driven organization with the unique blend of independent, trusted technical expertise; ongoing corporate and policy engagements; and a track record of reaching varied audiences.
 Key responsibilities
    (Technical version of role) Writing to the scientific community 
   Partner with our technical team early on in key research projects to identify the key narrative and message for their work.

  Edit drafts of academic papers to more effectively convey their ideas to a scholarly audience, and structure the papers to submission standards (including working in LaTeX where needed).

  Writing blog post summaries of papers, targeted at a technically knowledgeable (but not necessarily expert) audience (  example  ).

  Co-writing blog posts (  example  ), newsletters (  example  ) or position papers (  example  ) with our technical team to convey key positions or ideas.

 
   Content Strategy & Execution 
   Translate our core research findings into actionable insights for key non-technical audiences, e.g. policy briefs.

  Own written content on   FAR.AI  ’s website, our primary brand surface. Collaborate with our Digital Media Manager to shape the structure and presentation so it clearly communicates who we are and what we stand for.

  Own our quarterly newsletter, setting the editorial direction, consolidating key updates from across the team into a clear narrative for our key supporters.

 
   Voice, Narrative & Messaging 
   Work with our Communications Team Lead to establish and steward a consistent organizational voice, develop compelling narratives around our strategic priorities and key messages that support this narrative.

  Equip staff across all teams with the messaging, framing, and confidence to represent and amplify  FAR.AI ’s narrative in their own work and channels.

  Collaborate with our Digital Media Manager to ensure that our social media posts are consistent with this voice and narrative, including reviewing key posts.

 
  About You
 You are a skilled writer who is passionate about clearly communicating complex technical findings in a way that is actionable to diverse audiences. You combine crafting a compelling high-level narrative with hands-on execution and thrive in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment. You will be comfortable collaborating with key stakeholders across the organization to ensure  FAR.AI ’s messaging is always clear, persuasive, and credible. You will set the bar for clarity, accuracy, and rigor across  FAR.AI 's writing.
 Proactive and self-directed, you can carry several projects at once and bring each one over the finish line. You move fluidly between the rigorous and the accessible, and you treat clarity as a craft. Collaborative and detail-oriented, you make the researchers you work with sound like the best version of themselves.
 We welcome applications from both experienced writers, as well as technical specialist who are skilled and passionate communicators.
 We expect writers to have:
   3+ years of professional experience in a writing role (e.g., staff writer, science communicator, editorial lead).

  A portfolio of published work demonstrating their ability to turn complex technical material into clear, accurate writing (papers, technical reports, research blogs, or similar).

  We expect technical specialists to have:
   3+ years of experience in machine learning or a closely related field (e.g. maths, stats, physics) as a researcher or engineer (e.g. PhD in ML; Research Engineer).

  A portfolio of published writing across varying levels of complexity (two or more of: papers / technical documentation; blog posts; social media; op-eds; policy briefs).

  We expect all candidates to have:
   Proven ability to own projects independently from concept to completion.

    An interest in AI safety and our mission, and a willingness to learn.

  We expect strong candidates to have  some, but not all , of the following:
   Familiarity with the AI landscape and experience engaging with key stakeholders (governments, AI companies, policy think tanks).

  Strong working understanding of machine learning concepts, sufficient to represent research accurately and converse credibly with researchers.

  Experience with the academic publication process: arXiv, conference submissions, peer review, LaTeX.

  Track record of writing, ghostwriting and/or editing op-eds.

  Track record of writing to policymakers, e.g. policy briefs, especially in technology and innovation policy.

  Background in science journalism, research communications, or as a researcher who writes.

  Logistics
    Hours and Location : This is a full-time, long-term position that can be either in-person (Berkeley, CA; or Singapore) or globally remote (with overlap with 9am-noon Pacific time). We offer visa sponsorship for in-person employees.

   Compensation : We can offer compensation of $100,000–$200,000/year depending on experience and location, with the potential for additional compensation for exceptional candidates, plus our standard benefits for US & Singapore employees which includes catered lunch and dinner at our offices in Berkeley.

   Contractual Relationship : If based in the US or Singapore, you will be an employee of  FAR.AI  (501(c)(3) research non-profit / non-profit CLG). Outside the US or Singapore, you will be employed via an EOR organisation on behalf of  FAR.AI  or as a contractor.

   Application process:   Our application process includes a screening call, a paid 2-3h written test task, interviews with our team, and a paid full-day assessment. We expect filling out the initial application form will take less than 15 minutes.

  If you have any questions about the role, feel free to contact us at   talent@far.ai  . Otherwise, if you don't have questions, the best way to ensure a proper review of your skills and qualifications is by applying directly via the application form. Please don't email us to share your resume (it won't have any impact on our decision). Thank you!

title: Technical Writer
summary: The Technical Writer develops, maintains, and controls Field Service documentation for complex medical-device hardware systems. The role also establishes documentation standards, mentors junior writers and contractors, manages documentation workflows, and drives process and quality improvements through collaboration with engineering, product, training, and field-service teams.
description:
Company Description
 It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at  Intuitive . As a global leader in  robotic-assisted surgery  and  minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the  da Vinci surgical system  and  Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
 We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
 The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
 If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help  transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
 Job Description
  Primary Function of Position 
 As a member of the Services organization’s technical writing team, you’ll serve as both an independent contributor and leader in the development, delivery, and maintenance of Field Service documentation. This role combines hands-on technical writing with responsibility for establishing documentation standards, mentoring junior writers and contractors, and driving continuous improvement in documentation processes and quality.
 To be successful in this role, applicants must demonstrate independence in extracting and synthesizing complex technical information from systems, subject matter experts, field demonstrations, and laboratory environments. Strong technical judgment, combined with exceptional communication skills, enables this role to evolve with changing business needs while ensuring documentation remains accurate, clear, and usable, while staying compliant with company guidelines.
 This is an on-campus position with a minimum of 3 days a week in office and laboratory environments. Hands-on lab access is essential to this role’s effectiveness.
  Essential Job Duties 
  Plans, writes, edits, and maintains Field Service documentation (i.e., Field Service procedures) for medical device systems with strong independent technical judgment.
 Independently investigates and extracts technical requirements through systems review, laboratory demonstrations, engineering consultation, and field observation. Takes ownership of information gathering rather than relying on engineers to provide pre-written content.
 Establishes and maintains documentation standards, style guidelines, templates, and best practices. Develops and refines processes to improve team productivity and quality.
 Mentors and coaches junior writers and contractors. Provides technical feedback, reviews documentation, and contributes to team member development.
 Completes documentation control steps to release final documentation, tracking work in JIRA and maintaining Change Order records.
 Collaborates across product, engineering, training, and field service teams to ensure documentation meets end-to-end needs and aligns with company goals and quality standards.
 Evaluates and recommends process improvements, tooling enhancements, and workflow optimizations. Leads or participates in documentation infrastructure initiatives.
 Builds and maintains technical knowledge of Intuitive Surgical hardware systems sufficient to translate complex engineering concepts for field audiences.
  Qualifications
  Required Skills and Experience 
  5+ years technical writing experience for complex hardware and medical device products (installation, maintenance, troubleshooting, repair).
 Demonstrated ability to independently learn and understand mechanical systems through direct investigation and lab/field demonstrations.
 Expertise in minimalist hardware documentation using DITA XML tools (Oxygen XML Editor or equivalent).
 Professional writing samples must demonstrate technical depth, minimalist principles, and clear communication of complex concepts.
 Exceptional writing and analytical skills; ability to grasp, validate, and effectively communicate complex scientific and engineering concepts with technical rigor.
 Solid project-management skills; ability to manage multiple projects under tight deadlines and mentor others in project execution.
 Proficiency with current Adobe tools (Acrobat, Illustrator, InDesign, Photoshop) for documentation graphics.
 Medical device industry experience required. Field service or customer-facing documentation experience strongly preferred.
 Ownership mindset, commitment to quality and continuous improvement.
   Required Education and Training 
  Bachelor’s Degree in Technical Writing, Engineering, or related field required.
  Additional Information
 Due to the nature of our business and the role, please note that Intuitive and/or your customer(s) may require that you show current proof of vaccination against certain diseases including COVID-19.  Details can vary by role.
 Intuitive is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We provide equal employment opportunities to all qualified applicants and employees, and prohibit discrimination and harassment of any type, without regard to race, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, color, age, religion, protected veteran or disability status, genetic information or any other status protected under federal, state, or local applicable laws.

 For any Intuitive role subject to export controls, final offers are contingent upon obtaining an approved export license and/or an executed TCP prior to the prospective employee’s start date, which may or may not be flexible, and within a timeframe that does not unreasonably impede the hiring need. If applicable, candidates will be notified and instructed on any requirements for these purposes.

business need and/or on the selected candidate’s experience, knowledge and skills.
Compensation will be based primarily on the job level at which the role is filled and the
candidate’s qualifications, consistent with applicable law.
